title: Polymarket ‘surprised’ France blocked site as information source, plans legal challenge
summary: Last week, the ANJ ordered French internet service providers to block access to Polymarket ahead of the World Cup final.
full_text:
Polymarket ‘surprised’ France blocked site as information source, plans legal challenge
Quick Take
- The prediction market said it hasn’t allowed trading for French users since late 2024, but has allowed them to access Polymarket as an “information source.”
- Polymarket praised France for supporting technological innovation, but said it would legally challenge the blocking of its website.
We'd love your feedback.
France's gaming authority decided to block access to Polymarket's website, and now the prediction market says it plans to challenge that decision.
"We are disappointed by the French gaming authority’s (ANJ’s) sudden decision to unilaterally block our website — we intend to challenge this decision through the legal process in France," Polymarket said Wednesday.
Last week, the ANJ ordered French internet service providers to block access to Polymarket ahead of the World Cup final even though the prediction market had disabled trading there more than a year ago. Polymarket appears to have been taken aback by the decision.
"Polymarket has blocked trading from France since November 2024, but has continued to allow French users to access Polymarket as an information source," the firm said. "We were therefore surprised at the ANJ decision to block access to our entire website because their measure targets people going to Polymarket purely for information, not to trade."
The ANJ said in a statement Friday the site "is promoting an illegal gambling and betting offering" and could expose users to significant gambling losses, and that some wagers offered on it could be manipulated.
Although Polymarket said it banned French users from gambling, the site still drew 578,751 visits from 205,057 unique visitors in France in June, according to Similarweb data cited by the ANJ. The regulator added that Polymarket's homepage, despite being in view mode only, displays live odds and is therefore advertising gambling from an unauthorized service.
"We are proud that most people come to Polymarket solely to learn the probability of future events relevant to their everyday life with no intention to trade. Prediction markets help source truth," Polymarket said Wednesday.
While the world’s two biggest prediction market platforms, Polymarket and Kalshi, have been major successes in tech, achieving multibillion-dollar valuations and attracting loads of media attention, their rise has also been met with resistance. Many argue that the sites simply offer people ways to gamble on specific events. Regulators in both Europe and some U.S. states have sought to limit or ban the platforms.
Meanwhile, other stock and crypto trading platforms, including Robinhood and Coinbase, hope to make prediction markets a significant part of their revenue streams.

title: ‘Optimistic signals’ meet a $68,000 wall as bitcoin’s recovery faces its next test: analysts
summary: Bitcoin holds above $65,800 as spot ETFs log a sixth day of inflows. Bitfinex analysts flag $68K resistance as the next test.
full_text:
'Optimistic signals' meet a $68,000 wall as bitcoin's recovery faces its next test: analysts
Quick Take
- Bitcoin held above $65,500 on Wednesday as spot bitcoin ETFs extended net inflows to a sixth session, with the funds drawing roughly $779 million since July 13.
- Analysts put the next decision point near $68,000, where five months of underwater buyers sit at breakeven, and a first retest is expected to trigger heavy selling.
We'd love your feedback.
Bitcoin traded above $65,800 on Wednesday, its highest level in more than a month, as spot bitcoin exchange-traded funds extended a run of net inflows to a sixth straight session.
The funds drew $203 million on Tuesday, according to SoSoValue, whose figures cover U.S.-listed products only. Spot ether ETFs also added $37.5 million the same day, a third consecutive session of inflows.
Bitcoin (BTC) was up roughly 2% for the month on July 22, recovering ground after a quarter in which its two primary demand channels went quiet.
The wall at $68,000
Bitfinex analysts put the market's next decision point near $68,000, where the short-term holder cost basis and the second-quarter open have converged into a narrow band.
"Bitcoin remains capped by the Short-Term Holder Cost Basis near $68,000, which is the average cost basis for market participants over the last five months," the analysts wrote in the exchange's Alpha report published July 20.
This specific level matters because of who is sitting there — a cluster of underwater buyers.
A first retest is expected to catalyze a sharp response, the analysts wrote, as holders returning to their entry prices are historically the most prone to exiting at breakeven. Bitcoin closed its third consecutive positive week at $64,872, a 1.7% gain, and is up more than 11.5% over the three weeks since the start of July, according to the report.
A seasonally quiet tape
Vetle Lunde, head of research at K33, reads the same tape as seasonal rather than directional.
Bitcoin has entered a quiet summer phase, consolidating around $64,000 after reclaiming levels above $60,000, with July historically the weakest month of the year for bitcoin trading volumes.
Thirty-day spot volumes are running at 62.4% of the annual average as of July 19, closely tracking the seasonal pattern observed since 2020, according to K33 research. Trading activity typically bottoms around July 24.
The stabilization in ETF flows is the most encouraging development in that picture, Lunde wrote. In May, 70% of ETF trading days recorded net outflows, and in June that share reached 90%. So far in July it has fallen to 33%.
Bitcoin ETPs took in 778 BTC over the past week, bringing net inflows for July to 1,842 BTC on a global basis, according to K33. The final week of June saw weekly net outflows exceed 35,000 BTC, only the second time on record.
Yet, positioning is not stretched. CME open interest has stayed below 100,000 BTC throughout July, the lowest since October 2023, while the annualized one-month CME basis has firmed to a 5% to 7% range from 2% to 5% between mid-May and late June, the K33 report said.
A firmer basis alongside historically low open interest points to weak institutional participation rather than returning conviction, in Lunde's reading. Perpetual funding rates have recovered to an annualized 6% to 7% after turning negative in June, and the absence of positioning growth leaves little risk of a squeeze in either direction.
Bitcoin's 30-day volatility has fallen below 1.7% for the first time since May, with the asset consolidating between $62,000 and $65,000, according to the same report. K33 put the Fear and Greed index at 29, up from 23 a month ago.
One issuer carrying the bid
Analysts say the institutional picture is narrower than the headline flow numbers suggest.
Bitfinex counted four days of inflows totaling $500.2 million in the week to July 17, following a $424.7 million outflow that opened the week, with BlackRock's IBIT taking in $204.1 million while Fidelity's FBTC shed $181.1 million.
Excluding IBIT, the broader complex lost $128.6 million over that stretch, the report said. Institutional buyers have stopped redeeming without fully committing to reinvesting, in the analysts' assessment.
Yet, bitcoin's share of spot trading volume has climbed to nearly 67% from roughly 50% in June 2025, as ether cedes ground and SOL and XRP hold marginal share, according to Bitfinex. The firm reads that rotation as a de-risking phase rather than a broad return of risk appetite.
Institutional positioning
Open interest is flat on the week at roughly 474,000 BTC, and funding rates across major venues held in a tight, modestly positive band, according to Nexo analysts Dessislava Ianeva. She reads contained funding, steady ETF demand and stable spot flow as a market absorbing macro noise rather than showing stress.
Bitcoin needs to keep attracting inflows at an accelerating pace over a longer period to support the trend, Simon-Peter Massabni, head of business development at XS.com, said. He added that several upward attempts in recent weeks dissolved and gave way to renewed outflows.
Massabni also characterized it as too early to describe the market as accumulating rather than selling. The bid is arriving as equity investors reassess AI exposure. Massabni pointed to competition fears around Chinese models including Alibaba's Qwen3.8 Max and Moonshot's Kimi K3, which rattled related U.S. stocks late last week, alongside SpaceX shares closing 20% below their initial public offering price from last month.
Daniela Hathorn, senior market analyst at Capital.com, marked $63,000 as the level that has repeatedly drawn buyers. Holding above it would suggest the correction is stabilizing, she said, while a move back above $65,000 to $66,000 would improve momentum and strengthen the case for a run at recent highs.
"On the downside, a decisive break below support could trigger another wave of profit-taking," Hathorn shared with The Block.
What leads the next cycle
Bitwise Chief Investment Officer Matt Hougan once again looked past the bottom question entirely in a new memo, arguing the next crypto bull market will be defined by the convergence of onchain and traditional finance rather than by any single asset.
That means stablecoins, tokenization, round-the-clock trading, instant settlement and institutional DeFi scaling into the trillions, Hougan wrote. He expects the cycle to be the largest yet because it targets global finance rather than crypto alone, and because most investors are still asking whether crypto is over.
Two lanes in particular are best positioned in his view.
The first covers crypto applications with real revenue and tokenomics that tie token value to usage, with Uniswap, Aave and Morpho named alongside Hyperliquid, whose platform directs 99% of revenue to buying back its native token. Hougan said the token could double in price and still be fairly valued.
The second covers existing companies building on crypto rails, with Coinbase, Figure, BlackRock, Visa, Stripe, Robinhood and JPMorgan on his watchlist.
Robinhood Chain, the Layer 2 network the brokerage launched July 1, held more than $300 million in deposits and processed 3.6 million transactions a day within two weeks, a launch The Block reported at the time.

The Federal Reserve meets July 28-29, and both Bitfinex and K33 expect the rate to be held, with markets pricing a 15% probability of a hike.

Kyle Rodda, senior financial market analyst at Capital.com, argued bitcoin will serve as a barometer for how serious Warsh is about returning inflation to the 2% target.

title: Tokenized equity perps drive RWA trading boom to $470 billion monthly volume

full_text:
Tokenized equity perps drive RWA trading boom to $470 billion monthly volume
Quick Take
- Within the broader RWA category, tokenized equities have been the more popular asset class to trade over tokenized commodities.
- The following is an excerpt from The Block’s Data and Insights newsletter.
We'd love your feedback.
Tokenized real-world asset (RWA) perps have been the clearest crypto growth story of the year.
Monthly volumes across exchanges for these assets have grown from just $85 billion in January to around $470 billion in June, a 450% increase within just six months. The value prop for these products is clear: giving leveraged, 24/7, borderless exposure (and in Hyperliquid’s case, without KYC) to instruments that otherwise trade on limited hours in traditional, KYC-gated brokerages.
Within the broader RWA category, tokenized equities have been the more popular asset class to trade over tokenized commodities.
Tokenized equity perp volumes grew by roughly 7x from January to June, led by pre-IPO stocks such as SpaceX (SPCX), as well as single-stock semiconductor names such as MU, SNDK, SK-HYNIX and INTC, among others. SPCX was the single most-traded equity perp across all crypto exchanges in June with over $66 billion traded as it IPO'd in mid-June.
The dominant platforms facilitating RWA perps are quite concentrated at the top, with Binance, Hyperliquid and OKX making up over 80% of all tokenized RWA perps volume in June. Binance alone accounts for nearly half of all the category’s volume. Hyperliquid remains the standout onchain venue in an otherwise centralized field, while smaller onchain platforms like Ostium and Lighter sit well behind.

title: US Seizes More Than $25M in Crypto Tied to Investment and Romance Scams
summary: Prosecutors filed five forfeiture cases as Secret Service agents traced funds from thousands of victims to launderers in Southeast Asia.
full_text:
In brief
- U.S. prosecutors have seized more than $25 million in cryptocurrency linked to international fraud schemes that targeted victims across the U.S. and Canada.
- The money was recovered through five civil forfeiture complaints filed Tuesday in Washington, D.C., tied to investment and romance scams.
- It adds to the more than $800 million recovered by the Scam Center Strike Force, launched in late 2025.
U.S. prosecutors have seized more than $25 million in cryptocurrency tied to international scams that defrauded thousands of victims across the United States and Canada, the Justice Department said Tuesday.
The U.S. Attorney's Office for the District of Columbia, working with the Secret Service's Washington Field Office, filed five civil forfeiture complaints on Tuesday, each tied to a separate investigation into fraudulent crypto investment platforms and online romance schemes. Agents said they traced illicit proceeds through hundreds of intermediary wallet addresses, where they had been commingled with funds from other victims.
The largest complaint seeks some $12.1 million tied to romance scams that hit more than 200 people, followed by about $10.4 million flagged by Canadian authorities across more than 270 suspected victim transactions. The three remaining cases range from $285,000 to $2.4 million, including one in which scammers posed as recovery agents offering to retrieve funds stolen in an earlier fraud.
In each case, the launderers were mostly based in Southeast Asia, with IP addresses in China, Malaysia, and Cambodia, prosecutors said.
The Scam Center Strike Force
The seizure stems from the Scam Center Strike Force, launched in November 2025 by U.S. Attorney Jeanine Ferris Pirro. Investigators "cut through complex laundering schemes" to reach the money, Pirro said in a statement. The five investigations remain open, with the recovered funds bringing the strike force's total haul past $800 million.
In each case, prosecutors said, the launderers were mostly based in Southeast Asia, with IP addresses in China, Malaysia, and Cambodia—part of a scam economy increasingly run from the region and flagged by Interpol as a global threat.
Much crypto investment and romance fraud is operated out of forced-labor compounds in Cambodia, Myanmar, and Laos, where trafficked workers are coerced into defrauding victims worldwide. In October, U.S. and UK authorities charged Cambodia's Prince Group and seized more than 127,000 BTC from the network—then worth about $12 billion, marking the largest civil seizure and forfeiture in the DOJ’s history.

title: Centralized Elements 'Frequently Persist' in DeFi and Should Be Regulated: FATF
summary: Nearly every country has yet to apply the rules, the watchdog said, warning of outright bans for platforms that don’t comply.
full_text:
In brief
- The Financial Action Task Force said that many DeFi platforms are decentralized in name only and fall under its rules wherever identifiable people control them.
- Its report urges countries to find those controllers and regulate them as virtual asset service providers, and, as a last resort, to ban platforms that refuse to cooperate.
- Nearly 93% of surveyed jurisdictions have yet to apply the rules to qualifying DeFi arrangements, and just two have ever licensed or registered one.
Much of decentralized finance is not as decentralized as it looks, and the platforms behind it should be regulated like other financial businesses, the world's main anti-money-laundering body said in a new report.
In a report published Tuesday, the Financial Action Task Force said its rules already apply to any DeFi arrangement where an identifiable person keeps "control or sufficient influence," regardless of how decentralized a project claims to be. The Paris-based body, whose standards are used across more than 200 jurisdictions, sorts DeFi into three groups: platforms with identifiable controllers; those that are centralized in practice but whose operators stay hidden; and a genuinely leaderless minority it calls truly decentralized. Only the last escapes its standards.
Although many DeFi projects present themselves as fully decentralized, centralized elements "frequently persist in practice," the report found, through concentrated governance tokens, administrative privileges, control over upgrades, and the fees and rewards that flow to insiders.
FATF President Giles Thomson said in a statement accompanying the report that the goal is to stop criminals exploiting new technology to "launder dirty money" while "supporting responsible financial innovation," calling strong public-private information sharing central to the response.
Decentralized in name only?
The report lays out on-chain and off-chain signs of control, including upgrade keys and "kill switch" functions, the power to set fees or risk parameters, concentrated voting power, command of the public website or app, and the corporate entities that employ core developers or hold the treasury. Where such control exists, FATF said, the people behind it, whether developers, large token holders, front-end operators or funders, should be licensed and supervised like any financial firm. Even running a front-end that funnels users to a protocol can be enough to qualify.
In practice, almost no one is doing this. Nearly 93% of the jurisdictions that responded to a recent FATF survey have not applied the standards to any qualifying DeFi arrangement, and only 26 out of 142 have assessed the risks at all. Four have licensing rules on the books, while just two have ever used them to register or license a platform. FATF guidance is not law, but members are graded on how closely they follow it, and persistent gaps can help land a country on the watchdog's "grey list." The report comes on the heels of a broader FATF update days earlier that found most countries still struggling to enforce crypto rules across the board.
A ban as a last resort
FATF wants countries to close the gap by requiring, or at least encouraging, DeFi projects to build anti-money-laundering controls straight into their smart contracts or interfaces, from sanctions screening to proof-of-KYC checks before certain functions run.
For projects that really are leaderless, it steers regulators toward the choke points around them: stablecoin issuers that can freeze tokens, exchanges that handle fiat on- and off-ramps, and front-end operators. And where a platform refuses to cooperate, the report says, a jurisdiction can as a last resort ban it from operating in its territory. Banks and exchanges, for their part, are told to run due diligence on any DeFi platform they touch, or stop dealing with it.
North Korea's DeFi haul
The report leans heavily on how criminals already work the sector. It singles out North Korea, whose state-linked hackers it says were behind two April attacks that together drained more than $570 million: the $285 million exploit of Solana perpetuals exchange Drift Protocol, pulled off in just 12 minutes, and a $292 million hack of KelpDAO.
Together they made up some 76% of the year's crypto-hacking losses. The report also points to ransomware crews, professional laundering networks, and investor frauds as heavy users of DeFi's mixers, bridges and swaps.
That crackdown is already underway elsewhere. U.S. prosecutors this year secured prison terms for the two co-founders of Bitcoin mixer Samourai Wallet and a conviction against Tornado Cash developer Roman Storm, cases built on the same idea FATF presses here: that the people who build and run the code can be treated as regulated money businesses.
DeFi's total value locked reached $86.6 billion this year, up about 85% since 2023, with the top dozen protocols holding more than 60% of it, per the report, which calls for regulators to implement the FATF rulebook rather than leaving a gap that could enable illicit finance at scale.

title: OpenAI’s AI spending spree has ballooned to $750B
summary: OpenAI will spend the equivalent of Sweden's GDP on infrastructure through 2030.
full_text:
OpenAI announced Wednesday that it will spend $750 billion on infrastructure through 2030, some 25% more than it estimated earlier this year, The Wall Street Journal reported The renewed blitz comes as its Stargate data center project appears to have stalled.
The first salvo in OpenAI’s spending spree will be a $20 billion data center campus in Georgia known as Project Camellia. The development will span 1,400 acres northwest of Savannah and will draw at least 3.2 gigawatts of power from Georgia Power, the region’s utility. The generating capacity is expected to become available between 2028 and 2032.
The AI company said it would “pay the full cost of the infrastructure and electric-service costs” for the new data center. The Georgia Public Service Commission (PSC) adopted a rule last year to prevent utilities from passing on costs associated with new users drawing more than 100 megawatts.
Georgia Power also said OpenAI will reduce its power draw by up to 1 gigawatt during periods of high demand on the grid.
OpenAI is receiving a 50% property tax abatement for 15 years from Effingham County, according to the Effingham Herald.
Neither OpenAI nor Georgia Power has said how Project Camellia will be powered. TechCrunch asked both companies for specifics, but did not immediately receive a reply.
Regulatory filings might provide some clues. In December, Georgia Power received approval from the PSC to produce an additional 9,885 megawatts. The utility told the PSC it expects to have all the capacity contracted by the end of 2026. The OpenAI deal accounts for about a third of that.
Based on documents Georgia Power filed with the PSC, most of the new capacity will come from natural gas. The utility said it will build or buy from third parties about 5.8 gigawatts of natural gas generating capacity, about a quarter of which will be from more polluting simple-cycle turbines. Altogether, the new fossil fuel capacity will more than double Georgia Power’s natural gas fleet. The remainder will be supplied by grid-scale batteries and solar.
While electricity from Georgia Power is expected to start flowing in 2028, OpenAI did not give a timeline for when the first GPU will be turned on. That could happen sooner than 2028 given that OpenAI recently hired Brett Mayo to lead data center construction. Mayo previously worked at xAI, where he oversaw the Colossus data center in Memphis.
Colossus was built in record time, but it has allegedly taken its toll on local air quality, according to a lawsuit filed by the NAACP and the Southern Environmental Law Center. The xAI data center has been running dozens of unpermitted natural gas turbines, claiming exemption from federal clean air regulations.

title: If you pay a hacker’s ransom, chances are that they’ll come back for more
summary: The long-held understanding among security researchers and network defenders is that it's impossible to negotiate in good faith with an extortion racket because there's no incentive for the other side to actually walk away.
full_text:
Governments have long warned not to pay a hacker’s ransom demands, arguing that doing so only lets criminals profit from their cyberattacks and funds the next one. There’s also another reason: The hackers are unlikely to leave you alone if you pay up once, and many will come back demanding more.
In a report published Wednesday, cybersecurity giant Proofpoint said it surveyed 953 companies and found that over one-third of companies that paid a hacker’s ransom were hit with a second extortion demand. The findings underscore the long-held understanding among security researchers and network defenders that it’s impossible to negotiate in good faith with an extortion racket because there’s no incentive for the other side to actually walk away.
Proofpoint’s data shows that ransomware attacks and extortion attacks have evolved from a single transaction where hackers would get paid once and move on, into an effort using multiple forms of leverage, such as retaining stolen data under the threat of publicly releasing it.
While hackers have claimed in the past that they will delete or destroy the victim’s stolen data, past incidents have shown that not to be the case.
Last month, a hack at market research firm Klue exposed data belonging to its customers, including several cybersecurity firms. The company said it struck a deal with the hackers, who claimed to have deleted the data, but the company later conceded that a separate hacking group swiped a sample of the company’s stolen data, leaving its customers exposed to potential future extortion demands.
A similar situation befell Change Healthcare in 2024, after a Russian-speaking ransomware gang stole the health and medical data of the majority of people in America, some 192 million people. Amid a dispute between the hackers and their affiliates (criminal groups often subcontract out attacks), Change Healthcare paid separate ransoms to both groups of criminals to keep the sensitive medical data off of the internet.
Security researchers have long suspected that ransomware gangs and extortion rackets will keep hold of the victim’s stolen data, even after a payment is made. U.K. law enforcement confirmed this during their takedown efforts targeting the prolific LockBit ransomware gang in 2024. Police said that they found victims’ stolen data stored on LockBit’s servers long after they had paid the ransom.

title: What happens when you try to chop a photon in half?
summary: A mirror that moves mid-photon could release a shower of new photons.
full_text:
A photon is a single particle of light, and under normal circumstances, it can’t be divided. But a photon is also not a particle, in the sense that it does not have a specific location. Instead, it is an extended object.
So if a photon is only partway through the process of reflecting from a perfect mirror and you yank the mirror away, what happens? The answer, from a trio of Norwegian physicists, turns out (arxiv.org link) to be more complex than I expected.
A photon divided?
Let’s first talk briefly about dividing and combining photons. If this were a common experience in our lives, then shining a single color of light through a piece of glass or reflecting it from a surface might cause photons to divide or combine. This would lead to an amazing array of colors: Our universe would be the most fantastic and legal LSD trip you could imagine. But this doesn’t generally happen, hence LSD.
What does happen is that photons can divide and combine under the right circumstances—essentially, the medium through which the light travels has to change in response to the light. This can lead to a rainbow of colors from a single color source.
Technically, we would say that the light interactions we see around us are linear, and the combination/division of photons is a nonlinear process. Typically, to overcome that nonlinearity, you need either a very sensitive medium or a very high-intensity light source, like a laser.
The sudden removal of the mirror while a photon is reflecting is not nonlinear in the way that I would normally think about it. But if you give it more than a moment’s thought, it’s clearly a nonlinear event. This line of thinking is obscured by how we think about single photons at mirrors, though, as I will illustrate below.

title: Samsung unveils new Galaxy Z8 foldables and Galaxy Watches, available August 7
summary: Samsung's new foldables are slimmer, faster, and more expensive.
full_text:
The rumors haven’t left much to the imagination, but Samsung has unfurled its 2026 foldable lineup today. There are three models for the first time in Samsung’s eight-gen foldable family, including the top-of-the-line Z Fold 8 Ultra. That phone is the successor to last year’s Galaxy Z Fold 7, but the Z Fold 8 is new—the company’s first wide-body foldable designed for media over multitasking. And then there’s a new, thinner flip phone, plus a pair of smartwatches.
You can preorder Samsung’s new hardware today, but the component shortage has made these already spendy product lines more expensive this year. Even the Z Flip 8 is now well over a grand, and the Ultra costs almost twice as much.
The Z Fold 8 Ultra has the same basic form factor as the last few Samsung tablet-style foldables. A 6.5-inch OLED on the outside is about the same ratio as a standard smartphone screen. Open it up, and you get an 8-inch display that’s roughly twice as wide. That makes the main display close to square.
While the Ultra’s display is perfect for running two phone apps side by side, it’s not ideal for content consumption. The 5.5-inch cover display on the wider phone has a chunky 10:16 ratio. Unfold it, and the Z Fold 8 becomes a 7.6-inch 4:3 display. This gives widescreen videos a little more breathing room with smaller black bars, and it’s allegedly an ideal shape for reading documents in portrait orientation. Both the Ultra and wide-body Folds are impressively thin at 4.1 mm and 4.5 mm (unfolded), respectively.

title: Unlimited AI tokens aren't unlimited after all as US Army burns through supply
summary: Troops received an email informing them that they were rapidly depleting their AI tokens.
full_text:
A little over a month after the Department of Defense (DOD) bragged that nearly half of its 3.5 million employees were using AI at work, members of the Army’s Combat Capabilities Development Command (DEVCOM) received an email informing them that they were burning through tokens, and needed to limit use.
“Although the Army CIO announced in May 2026 that they were offering unlimited tokens, by mid-June the Army CIO pool was exhausted of tokens and had to re-establish limits,” the email reads. The email goes on to say that although the Army has chosen to renew token usage at “its current levels,” it’s unclear “if the Army CIO pool will be renewed after 1 Oct.”
The Army uses Ask Sage, a multimodal generative AI platform where users can run different large language models (LLMs), including Alphabet’s Gemini, Meta’s Llama, and OpenAI’s ChatGPT. “Apparently the whole Army burned through the whole year of tokens for just one service,” says an Army employee who spoke to WIRED anonymously because they were not authorized to speak to the press.
Ask Sage is used by the Army to “power its enterprise LLM workspace” and is “accredited for Controlled Unclassified Information.” It is also used by the DOD’s Chief Digital and AI Office (CDAO) for acquisitions. According to the Army’s website, Ask Sage was used to complete tasks like “reclassifying personnel descriptions, which involves defining and aligning job duties, experience and backgrounds.”
The Army employee says that the Army has been pushing its workers to lean into using generative AI. Employees were given an allotment of at least 200,000 tokens per month, according to emails viewed by WIRED, and were automatically allocated more if they burned through their initial allotment. Employees who had signed up for Ask Sage but were not regularly using it would receive emails encouraging them to use more of their allocated tokens.

title: Ukrainian drones deliver robots directly into battle by sea and air
summary: Ukraine's battlefield surge of robots now features airdrops and beach assaults.
full_text:
In the latest twist on battlefield innovations, Ukraine has used both flying drone carriers and drone boats to send ground robots armed with weapons or explosives into battle.
The drone-assisted deployments have enabled slower wheeled robots to bypass tough terrain and Russian defenses, and to carry out an unusual robotic amphibious assault on a contested position. Such tactics also showcase the Ukrainian military’s ongoing experimentation with using drones and robots to offset a Russian military advantage in manpower while also sparing Ukrainian soldiers from making dangerous assaults.
On July 19, a Russian military Telegram channel posted a video showing a Ukrainian hexacopter drone carrying a ground robot suspended below by a cable, according to the Ukrainian government-run news platform United24. The Russian Telegram channel described the Ukrainian heavy bomber drone as deploying a four-wheeled ARK-1 robot armed with explosive anti-tank mines on the ground where it continued toward Russian military positions—and apparently generated plenty of outraged comments from pro-Kremlin social media users.
It’s unclear how successful that particular mission was. But the tactic could improve the survivability of ground robots by helping them evade Russian aerial surveillance and drone strikes while closing with their targets more quickly. The ARK-1 robot can roll along at a top speed of nearly 28 miles per hour, although some robots are considerably slower.
Ukrainian ground robots also joined a Ukrainian military operation on June 25 that targeted the Kinburn Spit, a sandy and narrow peninsula that extends westward into the Black Sea and is connected to the Russian-occupied left bank of the Kherson Oblast.
Russian military forces captured the Kinburn Spit in June 2022 and set up positions there to help control southern Ukraine’s port access to the Black Sea, although they began withdrawing from the peninsula in early June as Ukraine’s mid- and long-range drone strike campaigns strained Russian supply lines.

— Eric Balchunas (@EricBalchunas) July 22, 2026
ETF 資金回流 7.5 億美元，BTC 漲幅傲視群雄
Balchunas 在貼文中以「生命跡象（SIGNS OF LIFE）」破題，指出自美國迎來 250 週年國慶日（7 月 4 日）以來，比特幣已強勢上漲了 8%。「它正在大幅跑贏（running circles around）其他所有資產，」他如此形容比特幣近期的強勁表現。
除了幣價的實質拉升，更令市場振奮的是機構資金的再度青睞。Balchunas 分享的數據顯示，比特幣現貨 ETF 的資金流也開始出現明顯的回流跡象，在過去一週內（截至發稿時）已錄得高達 7.5 億美元的淨流入。面對這波突如其來的漲勢，他坦言：「雖然很難完全相信它，但也很難想像它不會在某個時候反彈。我猜我們就拭目以待吧。」
分析師點名「OG 大戶」：你們是壓制幣價的濕毯子
有趣的是，Balchunas 在隨後的補充貼文中，將比特幣未能全面爆發的原因，歸咎於市場中早期參與者的拋售行為。他幽默地表示：「如果那些 OG（老派大戶）什麼都不做，它很可能就會反彈。」
他進一步指出，這些大戶在過去 9 個月裡，就像是一條「濕毯子（wet blanket）」一樣，死死壓制著比特幣的價格表現。為了加強語氣，他甚至引用了經典科幻電影《星際大戰》的台詞梗來調侃市場參與者：「在你回覆前，先感受一下自己的內心吧，Luke，你知道這是真的⋯⋯」

title: 加密金庫與借貸恐踩紅線？「加密老媽」Hester Peirce 示警：上鏈不等於脫離證券法
summary:
美國證券交易委員會（SEC）委員、被譽為「加密老媽」的 Hester Peirce 於 22 日發布最新聲明， […]

〈加密金庫與借貸恐踩紅線？「加密老媽」Hester Peirce 示警：上鏈不等於脫離證券法〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
美國證券交易委員會（SEC）委員、被譽為「加密老媽」的 Hester Peirce 於 22 日發布最新聲明，針對當前熱門的「加密金庫（Vaults）」與「鏈上借貸策略」發出監管提醒。她強調，雖然許多加密資產不屬於證券，但「代幣化證券仍是證券」，若金庫或借貸協議涉及主動管理、收益分配或決策引導，仍可能觸發聯邦證券法。Peirce 呼籲業者應主動與 SEC 對話，共同探索務實的合規路徑。
（前情提要：SEC加密老媽 Hester Peirce 力挺隱私工具：保護財務隱私等同守護國家安全）
（背景補充：加密老媽 Peirce 開講：開發區塊鏈只是在寫程式，不要把 Defi 代碼當證券）
美國監管機構對去中心化金融（DeFi）與鏈上收益工具的態度再度引發市場關注。台北時間 7 月 22 日，美國 SEC 委員 Hester M. Peirce 發布題為《倒立與夏日金庫：關於加密貨幣金庫與借貸策略的聲明》（Headstands and Summervaults: A Statement on Crypto Vaults and Lending Strategies）的公開文章，對當前蔚為風潮的加密收益工具劃出監管紅線。
上鏈不等於免監管！金庫與借貸策略面臨法律檢視
Peirce 在聲明中首先肯定了 SEC 過去一年半在釐清加密市場管轄邊界上的努力，認同許多加密資產與活動並不屬於聯邦證券法管轄範圍。然而，她特別強調：「代幣化證券仍是證券。」將證券活動轉移至區塊鏈上，並不會自動讓其逃脫證券法的約束。
針對近期熱門的「金庫（Vaults）」—— 即透過智慧合約自動將用戶資產分配至質押（Staking）或借貸等收益活動的工具，Peirce 指出其類型差異極大。若金庫完全由不可變智慧合約執行，性質較為純粹；但若有業者負責挑選收益策略、重新分配資產或指定決策者，就必須嚴格分析是否已觸發證券法規範。
同樣地，在鏈上「借貸策略（Lending Strategies）」中，如果管理者承擔了設定借貸利率、挑選可接受資產、決定貸款價值比（LTV）或清算門檻等職責，也應積極評估其法律風險。
四大潛在紅線：Howey 測試與票據認定
Peirce 詳細列舉了這類鏈上收益工具可能觸及證券法的幾種具體情境：
- 投資合約（Investment Contract）：若使用者投入資金，並期待從金庫部署者或策展人的創業與管理努力中獲利，將符合 Howey test 的證券判定標準。
- 票據（Notes）：視借貸行為的發行動機與推廣方式，相關借貸憑證可能被認定為證券（引用 Reves v. Ernst & Young 判例）。
- 投資公司法（Investment Company Act）：若金庫本身持有或投資證券，可能落入單位投資信託或管理型投資公司的監管範疇。
- 投資顧問規定（Investment Adviser）：管理金庫或引導借貸策略的行為，可能使其身份轉變為需受規管的投資顧問。
務實態度迎對話，喊話業者共創合規路徑
儘管劃出警示，Peirce 依然對這些新興工具的潛力表達了肯定。她認為金庫與借貸策略能協助投資人高效、低成本地管理資產並獲取收益，未來傳統證券上鏈後，更可能成為主流的投資組合管理工具。她同時強調，SEC 在分析時會尊重國會設定的權限界限，並保護開發者的言論自由。
在聲明結尾，Peirce 對 Web3 開發者與創新者發出真誠邀請。她鼓勵從事金庫設計或鏈上借貸的團隊主動聯繫 SEC，若經評估不在管轄範圍內固然良好；若涉及證券法，SEC 亦樂意共同探討如何在保護投資人與促進資本形成的前提下，尋求合規服務客戶的彈性途徑。

title: Benchmark 下調 Coinbase Q2 財報預測！分析師點出「Clarity Act」才是暴漲催化劑
summary:
據《The Block》報導，受加密市場第二季現貨交易量大幅下滑影響，Benchmark 分析師下調了對 Co […]

〈Benchmark 下調 Coinbase Q2 財報預測！分析師點出「Clarity Act」才是暴漲催化劑〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
據《The Block》報導，受加密市場第二季現貨交易量大幅下滑影響，Benchmark 分析師下調了對 Coinbase 的第二季財測與全年收入預估。然而，分析師強調 6 月交易活動已出現穩定跡象，更重要的是，若美國國會順利通過《Clarity Act》（加密市場結構法案），Coinbase 將成為最大受惠者，其長期正面影響遠勝於單季的疲弱財報。
（前情提要：Coinbase CEO 換掉大頭貼，Base 迷因幣 Brain 崩 93% 剩 140 萬鎂）
（背景補充：破紀錄！Coinbase 比特幣溢價指數連 60 天「處於負值」，美國機構買盤熄火）
隨著美國上市加密貨幣交易所 Coinbase 即將於下週公布第二季財報，市場對其營運表現的高度關注也隨之升溫。據《The Block》報導，知名投行 Benchmark 分析師 Mark Palmer 在財報出爐前夕，因應整體加密市場交易環境的艱難，下調了對這家美國最大加密貨幣交易所的營收預期；但他同時指出，一項潛在的監管法案可能成為推升股價的關鍵催化劑。
交易量驟降，Q2 收入預估遭下修
Palmer 在最新的報告中，將 Coinbase 第二季的收入預估從原先的 15.1 億美元，下調至 13.8 億美元；同時，他也將 2026 年的全年收入預估從 63.3 億美元，微幅調降至 60 億美元。
這項下修決定主要反映了第二季加密市場的嚴峻挑戰。數據顯示，在此期間，集中式交易所（CEX）的現貨交易量大幅下降約 28%，永續合約的交易活動也有所減少，而整體加密貨幣總市值更下跌了約 13%。基於這些因素，Benchmark 預測 Coinbase 的交易收入將面臨超過 5% 的衰退。
不過，Palmer 也帶來了一絲曙光。他觀察到 Coinbase 的交易活動在 6 月已趨於穩定，現貨交易量回升至 3 月以來首次超過 1 兆美元的水準，這項復甦跡象有望緩和整個季度表現疲軟的衝擊。
維持買入評級，Clarity Act 成最大利多
儘管短期財測遭下調，Benchmark 依然對 Coinbase 的後市抱持樂觀態度，維持其「買入（Buy）」評級與 270 美元的目標價不變。以報告發布時 Coinbase 約 172 美元的股價計算（年迄今下跌約 27%），這意味著該股仍有約高達 57% 的上漲空間。
文章強調，對投資者而言，比起單季的財報數字，更重要的是 2026 下半年加密市場的宏觀展望。Palmer 直言，目前市場尚未完全反映《Clarity Act》潛在通過所帶來的「選擇權價值（option value）」。他認為，一旦這項旨在建立美國全面加密市場結構的法案過關，Coinbase 將成為最大的潛在受益者之一。
值得注意的是，就在這份報告發布的前一天，美國總統川普已簽署相關的道德條款，為《Clarity Act》掃除最後的立法障礙。該法案預計將禁止聯邦官員發行加密貨幣，並將相關的執法權正式移交給司法部。Benchmark 總結指出，這項法案帶來的長期正面影響，其重要性將遠大於第二季弱勢財報，這才是真正能推動 Coinbase 股價重回上升軌道的主要動力。

summary:

〈RWA 代幣化股票市值飆漲 5 倍！a16z：AI 晶片成大熱門，傳統金融加速上鏈〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
代幣化股票（Tokenized Equities）正迅速崛起，成為區塊鏈領域成長最快的資產類別之一。據 a16z crypto 官方發布的最新市場分析，截至 2026 年 6 月，代幣化股票的總市值已達 17 億美元，較去年同期飆升逾 5 倍，且每月轉移量更暴增逾 170 倍。隨著 Coinbase、Binance 等巨頭紛紛入局，顯示加密貨幣技術正加速深入傳統華爾街市場。
（前情提要：A16z 創辦人 Marc Andreessen 進駐聯準會，AI 生產力任務組正式啟動）
（背景補充：a16z：AI新週期機器人上位，硬體狂飆軟體反轉）
在現實世界資產（RWA）的代幣化浪潮中，代表傳統股票、ETF 及指數的「代幣化股票（Tokenized Equities）」正迎來爆發性成長。據知名創投機構 a16z crypto 官方帳號發布的最新長文分析，代幣化股票憑藉著可自行保管、無需許可轉移、全天候交易以及可作為鏈上 DeFi 抵押品等優勢，正逐漸改變傳統金融市場的運作模式。
總市值達 17 億美元，新發行資產成主力
這份由 Robert Hackett 與 Ryan Holloway 撰寫的報告指出，截至 2026 年 6 月底，代幣化股票的總市值已攀升至約 17 億美元，相較於去年同期的 3.29 億美元，成長超過 5 倍，成為 RWA 中成長最快的類別之一。
值得注意的是，這波驚人的增長並非單純依賴底層股票價格的上漲，而是主要來自於大量「新發行」的代幣化資產。數據顯示，超過一半的當前市值來自一年前還不在鏈上的資產，而剩餘部分也大多是今年中才陸續上鏈的，顯示市場供給正快速擴張。
市場版圖大洗牌：AI 晶片類別成長最快
在過去一年中，代幣化股票市場的組成也經歷了劇烈變化。過去佔據主流地位的「加密連結產品」比例從 79% 大幅萎縮至 21%；取而代之的是，包含眾多長尾小資產的「其他類別」躍升至 35%，成為目前最大的類別。
與此同時，傳統科技巨頭也開始在鏈上發揮影響力。「大型科技股（Megacap Tech）」的佔比從微乎其微的 0.6% 攀升至 10.6%；而「ETF 與指數」類別也從 4.5% 成長至 17.3%。更令人矚目的是，受惠於全球人工智慧熱潮，「AI 與晶片類別」的佔比從不到 100 萬美元（0.3%）一路暴增至高達 15.5%，成為成長最為迅猛的細分領域。
機構巨頭爭相入局，每月轉移量飆破 92 億美元
伴隨著資產規模的擴大，交易活動也呈現井噴式成長。報告指出，2026 年 6 月代幣化股票的每月轉移量（包含交易、錢包轉帳及 DeFi 抵押等）達到了驚人的 92.2 億美元，相較去年同期的 0.53 億美元，成長超過 170 倍。
這股強勁的動能也吸引了眾多機構與平台在過去一個月內密集佈局：
- DTCC：在 Canton Network 上成功處理代幣化國債與股票的真實交易，並預計於今年 10 月全面推出，對接高達 114 兆美元的龐大資產。
- Robinhood：推出自家主網鏈，致力於將傳統市場、加密貨幣與 RWA 無縫整合。
- 紐交所（NYSE）母公司：與加密交易所 OKX 成立合資公司，計劃（待監管批准後）提供紐交所上市股票的代幣化版本。
- Coinbase 與 Binance：分別於 6 月中旬相繼宣布，將為非美國用戶提供與美股 1:1 錨定的股票代幣，且包含股息與完整股東權利，並支援 24/7 全天候交易。
a16z 在結論中強調，儘管目前 17 億美元的規模相較於每月交易量達數十兆美元的傳統股票市場仍顯得微不足道，但越來越多發行商與平台積極將股票代幣化的趨勢已十分明確。這股強勁的成長動能，正宣告著加密貨幣技術正以前所未有的速度深入華爾街的核心。

title: 球王梅西也看好世界模型！旗下基金投資李飛飛新創 World Labs，強強聯手 Nvidia 與 AMD
summary:
阿根廷足球巨星梅西（Lionel Messi）不僅在球場上稱霸，其投資版圖也正式跨足最前沿的人工智慧領域。據最 […]

〈球王梅西也看好世界模型！旗下基金投資李飛飛新創 World Labs，強強聯手 Nvidia 與 AMD〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
阿根廷足球巨星梅西（Lionel Messi）不僅在球場上稱霸，其投資版圖也正式跨足最前沿的人工智慧領域。據最新消息證實，梅西旗下的投資平台 Play Time HoldCo 已將由「AI 教母」李飛飛（Fei-Fei Li）所創辦的新創公司 World Labs 納入其投資組合中。World Labs 專注於開發「空間智能（Spatial Intelligence）」與世界模型，近期更獲得輝達（NVIDIA）、AMD 等科技巨頭的重金注資，估值高達約 50 億美元。
（前情提要：世界模型 World Model 是什麼？如何顛覆世界、運作原理、四大巨頭戰局與爭議）
（背景補充：Serenity：世界模型成 AI 圈最大共識，中國資金棄基礎模型，轉為物理AI）
在人工智慧技術從 2D 平面走向 3D 物理世界的關鍵時刻，頂尖體壇明星與科技先驅展開了跨界合作。由球王梅西於 2022 年在舊金山成立、規模約 2 億美元的投資平台 Play Time HoldCo，其官網近日明確列出已將知名 AI 新創 World Labs 納入投資組合。
AI 教母李飛飛操刀，專注「空間智能」
這筆投資之所以備受市場矚目，很大程度歸功於 World Labs 背後的靈魂人物 —— 被譽為「AI 教母」的華裔計算機科學家李飛飛。她不僅是史丹佛大學（Stanford University）人本人工智慧研究所（HAI）的共同主任，更是 2009 年 ImageNet 專案的創建者，該專案被廣泛視為推動現代電腦視覺與深度學習大爆發的關鍵催化劑。
李飛飛於 2024 年創辦的 World Labs，將研發火力集中於「空間智能」與「世界模型（World Models）」。有別於目前主流的大型語言模型（LLM），World Labs 的目標是讓 AI 能夠真正理解、生成並與真實的 3D 物理世界互動。目前，該公司已順利推出首款商用產品「Marble」，能夠透過文字、圖像或影片，一鍵生成可互動且可編輯的 3D 虛擬世界，未來將廣泛應用於創意設計、遊戲開發與機器人等領域。
獲輝達、AMD 巨額注資，估值上看 50 億美元
World Labs 在資本市場上的吸金能力同樣令人咋舌。自 2024 年 9 月以 10 億美元估值完成 2.3 億美元的首輪融資後，該公司隨即在 2026 年 2 月完成了規模高達 10 億美元的新一輪鉅額融資。
在這輪融資中，不僅獲得了輝達（NVIDIA）與 AMD 等晶片巨頭的青睞，更由知名軟體大廠 Autodesk 領投 2 億美元並出任顧問，富達（Fidelity）與 Emerson Collective 亦參與其中。這使得 World Labs 的累計融資額突破 12 億美元，市場傳聞其最新估值已飆升至 50 億美元左右。
梅西的前瞻佈局：體育與 AI 的交叉融合
透過 Play Time HoldCo 的這步棋，梅西展現了對長期財富規劃與未來科技趨勢的敏銳嗅覺。除了 World Labs 之外，該平台的投資組合還包含了 FieldAI（機器人）、Fish Audio（語音 AI）以及 SuperAnnotate（AI 數據平台）等多家前沿科技公司。
梅西將自身的全球影響力與科技產業深度結合，選擇與輝達、Autodesk 等巨頭在同一個頂級賽道上押注「世界模型」，這不僅為 Play Time HoldCo 帶來了極具前瞻性的戰略地位，也讓外界看見了體壇資本在推動下一代人工智慧發展中所扮演的全新角色。

title: 黃仁勳霸氣挺中國 AI！稱美國陷入 Kimi 恐慌「搞錯重點」：免費開源將引爆 NVIDIA 晶片需求
summary:
針對近期中國 AI 模型 Kimi K3 所引發的市場恐慌，輝達（NVIDIA）執行長黃仁勳給出了截然不同的解 […]

〈黃仁勳霸氣挺中國 AI！稱美國陷入 Kimi 恐慌「搞錯重點」：免費開源將引爆 NVIDIA 晶片需求〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
針對近期中國 AI 模型 Kimi K3 所引發的市場恐慌，輝達（NVIDIA）執行長黃仁勳給出了截然不同的解讀。據《Axios》獨家專訪，黃仁勳強烈捍衛中國開源 AI 模型，認為美國企業「絕對」應該使用這些優秀模型。他直言華爾街與華府的封殺心態完全搞錯方向，因為更便宜、開源的 AI 應用將大幅推升對硬體與晶片的強勁需求。
（前情提要：Sega 當年如何救輝達一命？讓黃仁勳感念了整整 30 年）
（背景補充：黃仁勳穿過的原味招牌皮衣想入手？蘇富比舉辦慈善拍賣，估價曝光）
中國新創 Moonshot AI 推出的 Kimi K3 模型近期震撼市場，憑藉著近乎前沿的性能與極低價格，引發了自 2025 年 1 月 DeepSeek 事件以來最嚴重的晶片股拋售恐慌。然而，在全球 AI 算力霸主輝達（NVIDIA）執行長黃仁勳的眼中，這場「Kimi 恐慌」完全是一場誤會。
華府搞反了，免費 AI 是硬體的超級利多
在德州沃斯堡（Fort Worth）出席由台灣代工大廠緯創所建設的先進 AI 基礎設施廠開幕式時，黃仁勳接受了《Axios》的獨家專訪。他直白地表示，華爾街與華府對於中國開源 AI 模型的恐懼「完全搞反了」。
他解釋道，更便宜且開源的模型會促使更多人與企業接觸人工智慧，進而擴大整個市場規模；而這些應用的普及，最終將無可避免地轉化為對輝達晶片、資料中心與運算能力的強勁需求。「免費 AI 應該對硬體是好事，對晶片是好事，對資料中心是好事，」黃仁勳強調。
反對國安封殺，直言「中國不可能把美國趕出賽道」
近期，包含美國財政部長 Scott Bessent 在內的川普政府官員，以及部分美國 AI 實驗室，紛紛指控中國模型透過「蒸餾（distillation）」竊取美國技術，並積極遊說華府祭出制裁與封鎖。
對此，黃仁勳表達了明確的反對立場。他指出，從其他知識來源學習與蒸餾是「智能的基本要素」，政府應該懲罰具體的違規行為，而不是針對模型本身進行打壓。針對外界擔憂的「北京後門」風險，他駁斥這是一種誤解，因為企業完全可以在安全的「沙盒（sandbox）」環境中自訂並監控模型的使用。他更霸氣宣示：「在任何情境下，中國都不可能把美國公司趕出賽道。零可能性。」
開源讓 AI 更安全，籲 Anthropic 解禁模型
黃仁勳進一步提出反直覺的觀點：基於國家安全理由限制開源模型，反而會讓美國變得更加脆弱。他深信「開放」能讓全球外部研究人員檢驗模型、找出弱點並建立防禦，「如果全世界只剩單一模型、單一點攻擊、單一故障源，整個世界會脆弱得多。」
他甚至將這套開放邏輯應用在美國同業身上，公開呼籲人工智慧巨頭 Anthropic 應該將其限制存取的網路安全模型 Claude Mythos 開放給「所有人」使用，透過快速測試與修復來強化防禦，而非從一開始就設下限制。黃仁勳總結，這場 AI 競賽並不是一場「有終點的賽跑」，美國與中國都將長期存在，而擁抱開放將是加速整體 AI 產業成長的最佳解方。

• 黃仁勳認為美國對中國開源AI模型的恐懼是誤解，免費的AI應用將推升對輝達晶片的需求。

title: 比特幣見底了？交易員 KillaXBT：已完成 5 波熊市修正，但「這指標」提早了 100 天
summary:
比特幣（BTC）是否已經真正觸底？據知名加密貨幣交易員 Killa 於 X 平台發布的最新技術分析指出，比特幣 […]

〈比特幣見底了？交易員 KillaXBT：已完成 5 波熊市修正，但「這指標」提早了 100 天〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
比特幣（BTC）是否已經真正觸底？據知名加密貨幣交易員 Killa 於 X 平台發布的最新技術分析指出，比特幣目前已經完成了歷史熊市常見的「5 波修正」結構，從形態上來看底部可能已經確立。然而，他同時警告，本次修正週期僅花費約 260 天，比過去平均提早了近 100 天，因此對見底時機仍抱持 50/50 的保留態度，呼籲投資人做好迎接市場震盪的準備。
（前情提要：資金逃離 AI 轉進比特幣？Wintermute：加密市場展現相對強勢，但須留意通膨反撲）
（背景補充：比特幣衝破 6.6 萬是「槓桿幻象」？CryptoQuant 分析師警告：現貨買盤並未跟上）
隨著加密貨幣市場持續在低點震盪，投資人最關心的莫過於「比特幣（BTC）到底跌完了沒？」台北時間 7 月 22 日，在 X（前 Twitter）上擁有高關注度的交易員 Killa（@KillaXBT）發布了一篇深度的市場觀察報告，透過覆盤歷次熊市週期的規律，為當前的比特幣走勢提供了全新的技術分析視角。
I observed every single $BTC bear cycle.
Key update:
Practically every single cycle, we complete a 5-wave correction. We also tend to form two significant bear market highs. The first comes immediately after the initial top on the first major retrace. This is the complacency… pic.twitter.com/QrJYOSW5q9
— Killa (@KillaXBT) July 22, 2026
5 波修正與「自滿高點」的誘惑
Killa 在貼文中指出，根據他的長期觀察，幾乎每一個比特幣熊市週期都會經歷完整的「5 波修正（5 waves of correction）」，並且在這個過程中，通常會形成兩個極具欺騙性的重要熊市高點。
他特別點出，第一個高點往往出現在初始高點後的第一次主要回檔，這被稱為「自滿高點（complacency high）」。在這個階段，市場情緒通常會被短暫的拉升所蒙蔽，導致大多數散戶誤以為「牛市已經回來了」而盲目追高。Killa 坦言，正是因為精準捕捉到了這一輪的自滿高點，他才得以成功從 9.6 萬美元一路做空至 7 萬美元，獲取了豐厚的利潤。
死貓反彈後，結構顯示底部已現
回顧歷史數據，Killa 發現 2014 年、2022 年以及當前的 2026 年，比特幣走勢都出現了極為相似的結構：在自滿高點過後，價格會繼續向下創出新低；即便是沒有創新低的 2018 年，整體結構也包含了多次向下回測。
他進一步解釋，在經歷這些下挫後，市場通常會出現所謂的「死貓反彈（dead cat bounce）」，藉此建立起堅實的「基礎低點」。此時往往是市場情緒最為絕望的時刻，散戶瘋狂做空，隨後引發 Delta 翻轉與空頭擠壓（Short Squeeze），進而帶動價格強勢反彈。
對於當前的市場狀況，Killa 抱持樂觀態度。他認為比特幣已經成功掃過了死貓基礎低點，並徹底完成了與過去歷史相同的 5 波修正結構。單從形態結構上來看，比特幣的底部似乎已經正式浮現。
時間指標成隱憂：提早了 100 天？
儘管結構上發出了強烈的見底訊號，但 Killa 心中仍有一絲猶豫，而這個隱憂來自於「時間因素」。
他指出，過去幾次熊市從最高點跌至最終底部，大約都需要耗時 365 天。然而，如果目前的價位真的就是本輪熊市的最低點，那麼這次從高點到底部僅花費了約 260 天，足足比歷史平均早了近 100 天。
正因如此，Killa 目前對市場抱持著「50/50」的中立態度：結構分析顯示底部可能已經到來，但時間指標卻暗示時機或許還未完全成熟。不過他也強調，市場週期的長度最終是會改變的，不能假設歷史永遠一成不變。展望未來，他預期接下來市場可能會經歷一段震盪期，但相較於大幅跌破前低，更有可能形成「更高低點（higher low）」。最後他也不忘提醒，這僅是個人的技術分析分享，並非財務建議（NFA），呼籲投資人務必做好風險控管。

title: Most bus fares in England to be capped at £2 from January
summary: The government says the policy will "help with the cost of living and give people the breathing space they need"
full_text:
Most bus fares in England to be capped at £2 from January
- Published
The bus fare cap in England will revert to £2 from January, new prime minister Andy Burnham has announced.
The government says the policy, which is expected to cost more than £500m, will "help with the cost of living and give people the breathing space they need".
At the start of last year, the England-wide bus fare cap rose to £3 under Sir Keir Starmer's Labour government, although in Liverpool and Manchester fares were held at £2.
Burnham said affordable transport links were an essential, adding: "Lower fares will help people get to where they need to."
The measure gives people "a little bit of hope" in a time when many are grappling with higher living costs - especially after fuel costs spiked as a result of the US-Iran war, transport secretary Heidi Alexander told the BBC's Today programme.
However, she admitted the measure was "not the whole solution".
The new cap will take effect from January next year for fares on participating buses outside of London. The cost of a non-discounted single bus journey in London is £1.75.
The Burnham government said going back to a £2 cap should particularly help passengers in rural and coastal areas, where single fares can be higher.
The Campaign for Better Transport said rural areas were still suffering from fewer bus routes and services, adding that such areas had been more affected by council cut backs in the last decade than urban zones.
Services in those areas - as measured by vehicle miles - decreased by 18% between 2019 and 2024, according to the County Councils Network, which represents 39 unitary and county councils across England.
"What we need to see is the replacing of those lost services which have particularly affected those in rural areas," Campaign for Better Transport's Michael Solomon Williams said.
What about N Ireland, Scotland and Wales?
In other nations, public services in Northern Ireland will also get a small amount of additional money, though ministers will not be obliged to spend the money on public transport. The exact amount will not be known until the autumn budget.
Scotland and Wales will get equivalent funding to England for the bus fare cap scheme.
The Scottish government, which piloted a £2 bus fare cap across the Highlands and Islands for a year, said it was looking at bringing forward legislation for a £2 bus fare cap across the whole of Scotland by the end of this parliament.
Single fares are already limited to £1 for under 21s in Wales.
Bus use still lower post Covid
When first introduced in 2023, the £2 cap was initially meant both as a cost of living measure and to encourage people back onto buses in the wake of the pandemic.
It played a role in reducing inflation that year, the Office for National Statistics said.
An evaluation of the first ten months found that the scheme contributed 5% of the 13% rise in bus usage during that period. Lower-income passengers felt the most financial benefit.
However it did not score highly when it came to value for money. How much money people saved varied depending how much fares in their local area cost before the cap.
In those first ten months, £210m was spent on the scheme, less than the £245m budget.
Even if fare-capping measures had increased demand for bus travel, numbers are still recovering from the huge drop in usage during Covid.
By March 2025, 1.9 billion journeys were made on local buses in England outside of London - around 93% of pre-pandemic levels.
- I travel four hours on a bus per day - the bus fare cap will save me £500 a year - Published3 hours ago
 
Shadow Chancellor Mel Stride said the government has not actually specified where the money will come from to fund the bus fare cap extension.
"That is a worrying sign, we need to have a government which is on top of the public finances, not one that is making lots of spending commitments without explaining where the money is going to come from," Stride told BBC Breakfast.
In its announcement, the government said £454m will be reallocated from the Department for Energy Security and Net Zero (DESN).
DESN says this will be used in addition to funds already earmarked by the Department for Transport for buses.
Alexander told the BBC it was money that had been allocated in DESN's budget to spend on international climate projects.
"And so instead of putting that money out as grants we are going to be issuing loans and so that money comes back in," she said.
It is the second day in a row that the new prime minister has announced cost saving measures, following Tuesday's VAT cut on household electricity bills later this year.
In his first cabinet meeting on Tuesday, Burnham promised to lead a "cost of living government", telling ministers that he wanted to give people a "sense that help is coming" on costs.

title: Tankers make sharp U-turns after Houthi shipping threat
summary: All of the ships were travelling to or from Saudi ports before changing course, ship-tracking data shows.
full_text:
Tankers make sharp U-turns after Houthi shipping threat
- Published
At least seven oil tankers have made U-turns close to Yemen since the Iran-linked Houthi group announced a "maritime embargo" against Saudi Arabia on Monday, ship-tracking data shows.
All of the ships were travelling either to or from Saudi ports and made sharp changes of course after the embargo was announced.
Nearly 15% of global sea trade moves through the Red Sea, which connects the Mediterranean and Gulf of Aden through two choke points - the Suez Canal in Egypt and the Bab al-Mandab Strait between Yemen and the Horn of Africa.
The Red Sea has been a key route for exports of Saudi oil since the US-Israeli war with Iran led to the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz, which has severely restricted the flow of oil and gas from the Gulf.
This has played a "major role in relieving pressure to global markets" and if the Houthis further restrict trade then "prices will go up", said Rosemary Kelanic from the US-based Defense Priorities think tank.
The day before the Houthis announced their blockade, 20 vessels entered the Red Sea and 22 exited via the Bab al-Mandeb strait, according to maritime intelligence firm Kpler.
Kelanic told BBC Verify that any Houthi attacks on vessels in the Red Sea or Gulf of Aden "will suppress all international traffic not just Saudi-bound vessels".
The EU's naval force in the region Aspides recommended on Wednesday that "merchant vessels linked to Israeli, US or Saudi interests avoid transiting the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden until the threat level decreases", according to an advisory seen by Reuters news agency.
Ship-tracking data from MarineTraffic shows the crude oil tanker Rodos, loaded with Saudi crude, departed for India from the Red Sea port of al-Muajiz on Monday evening. The Liberian-flagged ship set off south towards the Bab al-Mandab Strait but about nine hours later made a U-turn and began sailing north instead.
The Liberian-flagged oil and chemical tanker Mica departed Saudi Arabia's Jazan port on Monday afternoon and also headed south before reversing course.
Ship-tracking data shows at least eight ships bound for the Red Sea have made U-turns instead of entering the Bab al-Mandab Strait from the south as well.
Marshall Islands-flagged vehicle carrier Liu Jiang Kou was sailing to Saudi Arabia's Jeddah port from China before completely changing course on Monday in the Gulf of Aden.
A Hong Kong-flagged crude oil tanker sailing from China called New Prime also turned around as it headed towards Saudi Arabia on Monday and now appears to be waiting in the Arabian Sea.
While the reasons for each course change cannot be independently verified, "the timing is consistent with the embargo announcement," said maritime risk management company Vanguard.
In an email to shipowners on Monday, which the BBC has seen, the Houthis said "vessels are banned from loading or discharging cargo at any Saudi ports". It added that ships "may be subject to targeting in any location within the operational reach".
The Houthis have said their embargo is in retaliation to a Saudi blockade of ports and airports in Houthi-controlled north-western Yemen.
Saudi Arabia has condemned the allegation and has vowed to "take all necessary measures to protect its ships in accordance with international law".
Yemen has been devastated by a civil war since 2014, when the Houthis captured the capital of Sana'a from the government. The conflict escalated in 2015, after a Saudi-led coalition of Arab states intervened to try and restore the official government.
There has been an informal truce between the Houthis and Saudi Arabia since 2022. But last week, the Houthis launched missiles at an airport in south-western Saudi Arabia in response to air strikes on Sanaa's airport that they blamed on the kingdom.
The Houthis have previously caused severe disruption to the the 32km-wide (20-mile) Bab al-Mandab Strait.
Shortly after the Gaza war broke out in October 2023, the Houthis began attacking merchant vessels in the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden, saying they were acting in support of the Palestinians. These attacks led to four ships being sunk, one vessel seized, and nine crew members killed.
Since the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, Saudi Arabia has diverted more than 70% of its crude exports from the Gulf to the Red Sea port of Yanbu through an east-west pipeline.
About four million barrels per day have been shipped from Yanbu in recent weeks, compared with about 973,000 a year earlier, according to data from Kpler and maritime analytics platform Signal Ocean.
Naveen Das, a senior oil analyst from Kpler, told BBC Verify the only option left to the Saudis if the Bab al-Mandab Strait is effectively closed would be to move oil all the way through the Mediterranean and around the southern tip of Africa to get to Asia.
The impact of the blockade on consumers won't be immediate, but the conflict with Iran has made the global energy system more vulnerable to shocks like these, Das added. "We could weather it for two weeks, three weeks, even a month, but even in that time, we will see higher freight rates, higher energy prices and that bleeds into higher energy consumer costs."
Ships close to the Red Sea are also broadcasting messages in an attempt to deter attacks, a common practise in the region since the Houthis targeted vessels during the war in Gaza.
At least 50 vessels in the region are broadcasting they have armed guards on board, according to data from MarineTraffic.
Martin Kelly, from crisis management firm EOS Risk Group, told BBC Verify that captains will fear the "Houthis might read your situation wrong" and think their ships have "called at a Saudi port in the past, then therefore you could be attacked".
"A lot of these ships are very large crude oil carriers. I think the damage would be catastrophic. There would be certainly be deaths onboard these ships," he added.
Additional reporting by Barbara Metzler

title: Seized maternity notes not given to Lucy Letby defence for trial, BBC learns
summary: A BBC File on 4 investigation has uncovered what one professor said was a "very surprising" omission.
full_text:
Seized maternity notes not given to Letby defence for trial
- Published
Maternity notes for the babies Lucy Letby has been convicted of murdering were not made available to her defence ahead of her trial, the BBC has learned.
The neonatal nurse was convicted of murdering and attempting to murder 14 babies at the Countess of Chester Hospital in 2015 and 2016.
File on 4 Investigates has discovered that maternity notes for the babies in the case - which include details of the mother's pregnancy, labour and birth - were seized by Cheshire Police. But they were not reviewed by the prosecution's chief medical expert or disclosed to Letby's defence.
The Crown Prosecution Service said Letby was convicted following two jury trials and that the Court of Appeal dismissed her argument that prosecution evidence was flawed.
Letby, originally of Hereford, is currently serving 15 whole life terms.
Since her trial, and subsequent retrial on one case, there have been concerns raised about some of the evidence presented to the jury.
One concern is that the maternity history of the babies in the case was not adequately considered.
Experts told the BBC that it is critical to fully assess the pregnancy, labour and delivery of a baby when determining why they collapsed and died.
Dr Dewi Evans, the chief medical witness for the prosecution, said the full maternity notes were not relevant to the case.
"I never saw any obstetric notes and I have no idea what happened to them," he said.
"I don't think that maternity care was a particular issue in the Letby case. I think most of the babies I dealt with were born in acceptable condition."
Evans said he did see brief maternity summaries - "usually a couple of paragraphs" - attached to each baby's neonatal notes.
File on 4 Investigates has also learned from several sources that the Crown Prosecution Service did not disclose the obstetrics records to the defence.
The CPS reasoned that because the prosecution did not use them to form its case against Letby, they were not relevant.
The BBC has also seen evidence the defence did request the maternity notes but they were not released.
Evans said the CPS should have disclosed the records, even if the prosecution was not using them.
He added: "With the benefit of hindsight, would that have made a difference to the outcome? I don't think so. The events that occurred to these babies were events that occurred after they were born."
However, Phil Bennett, professor of obstetrics and gynaecology at Imperial College London, disagreed.
"It's very surprising indeed to me that little or no attention was paid to the maternity care in these cases," he says.
He said that when investigating a baby's death in a hospital or as part of litigation, it is normal practice for maternity care and neonatal care to be considered together.
"These experts should know that to come to the right conclusion you need an integrated opinion," he added.
Bennett has reviewed one case, referred to in court as Baby O, in detail on behalf of her new defence.
The jury unanimously convicted Letby of murdering the triplet after the prosecution said she had injected air into his bloodstream, into his feeding tube and inflicted liver damage.
Bennett relied on Baby O's neonatal notes as well as testimony from a police interview with the baby's mother about the infant's birth.
The prosecution argued that Baby O was born in good condition and was stable for 48 hours before he suddenly collapsed. They said that indicated that Letby attacked him.
But Bennett's opinion is that the baby died from a liver condition caused by an injury to his liver during, what he believed was, a difficult Caesarean section to deliver him.
He says though this is quite rare, there was substantial medical literature on it.
In these medical reports the injury usually happened during delivery and the baby seemed to be well for an average of 48 hours until suddenly collapsing and often dying.
Bennett said he would like to see the obstetrics notes to get a better understanding of the delivery.
In response, Evans said Baby O was born in good condition.
He added: "I don't think that anything in the obstetric notes would have improved my understanding or the understanding of all of us who became involved with this investigation."
File on 4 Investigates spoke to various families who alleged failings of care on the maternity and neonatal units at the Countess of Chester, before during and after Letby's time at the hospital.
None of them encountered Letby.
'Significant improvements'
They said doctors, nurses or midwives repeatedly ignored their concerns about the progress of their labour or the health of their baby. In several of these cases their babies died.
Sue Pemberton, the deputy chief executive of the Countess of Chester, said they "apologise unreservedly to the families who have had poor experience in our care".
She said she noted that the cases being discussed relate to maternity care between 2015 and 2020 and that if families felt their concerns had not been addressed she would urge them to contact the trust.
She said: "The Trust has made significant improvements and it is now nationally accredited for its family-integrated care approach."
The Crown Prosecution Service said: "Lucy Letby was convicted of 15 separate counts following two jury trials.
"In May 2024, the Court of Appeal dismissed Letby's leave to appeal on all grounds – rejecting her argument that expert prosecution evidence was flawed."
Cheshire Constabulary said it would not be commenting.

title: Wreckage of Pan Am plane that shaped aviation safety found 74 years on
summary: The deaths of 52 people on the Clipper Endeavor led to the introduction of mandatory pre-flight safety briefings.
full_text:
Wreckage of Pan Am plane that shaped aviation safety found 74 years on
- Published
The wreckage of a Pan American Airways plane has been found 74 years after it plunged into the Atlantic Ocean in a crash that prompted mandatory airline safety briefings.
The Clipper Endeavor was found 2,000ft (610m) below sea level off the coast of Puerto Rico with a sonar-equipped drone. It went down on 11 April 1952 following multiple-engine failure shortly after take-off.
Everyone onboard survived the impact - but passengers struggled to locate life vests and rafts as the plane rapidly sank. Of the 69 passengers and crew onboard, just 17 survived.
The disaster led to sweeping reforms in aviation safety, including compulsory pre-flight safety briefings on every commercial flight.
The expedition to find the wreckage was led by the Air/Sea Heritage Foundation in partnership with the Discovery Channel's Expedition Unknown show and several other organisations.
Last month, explorers discovered the ruins of the Douglas DC-4 aircraft using an autonomous sonar drone that detected the aircraft's fuselage and tail.
"We are all stunned and elated by this discovery, yet also humbled to remember what happened in that place so long ago," said Russ Matthews, president of the Air/Sea Heritage Foundation.
The plane had been carrying 64 passengers and five crew to New York when the pilot was forced to make a violent water landing.
The confusion that ensued became a "catalyst" for modern regulations mandating better flotation equipment on planes and preflight briefings on how to use it, aviation safety expert John Cox told AP.
Today, before every commercial flight, cabin crew are required to outline where a plane's exits are, as well as the location of life vests and how to inflate them.
"Every time you step onboard an airplane today, you are safer because of what happened to Clipper Endeavor and her passengers three-quarters of a century ago," said Expedition Unknown host Josh Gates.
Matthews, a maritime explorer and historian, first became interested in the crash in 2019, after reading about a luggage tag from the flight that had washed ashore in Florida.
He said in a statement that he had been "astonished that such an important story had largely faded from public memory".
He then began piecing together the aircraft's final moments using reports from the Civil Aeronautics Board, the predecessor to the US Federal Aviation Administration.
The breakthrough came after researchers uncovered records from a public hearing in Puerto Rico, including a map drawn by air force pilots who had witnessed the crash, which helped narrow down the search area.
Researchers used historical records and weather data from the time of the crash to identify the 10 square nautical miles of Atlantic Ocean seabed where the wreckage was likely resting.
An attempt to locate the wreckage in 2024 was abandoned due to poor weather - but Matthews said his team had been determined to return before the 75th anniversary of the crash.
A drone found the wreckage - which had broken into two sections - during its first pass of the search area on 2 June.
A follow-up photographic survey confirmed the wreckage was of the Clipper Endeavor, providing images that revealed the Pan Am logo and aircraft's name were still visible on the fuselage.
"To have a front-row seat to an expedition like this as it's unfolding is tremendous, and so I feel really lucky that we were able to be a part of it," said Gates, who was aboard the surface ship when the wreckage appeared on screen.
The discovery could offer fresh hope for the families of passengers of other planes that are presumed to have crashed in the ocean, such as Malaysia Airlines Flight 370.
It disappeared 12 years ago with 269 people onboard and, despite numerous searches in the Indian Ocean, has not yet been located.
The discovery of the Clipper Endeavor will be featured in a special episode of Expedition Unknown this Autumn.

title: Who is Mykhailo Drapatyi, Ukraine's new commander-in-chief?
summary: Drapatyi becomes Ukraine's third commander-in-chief since Russia's full-scale invasion in February 2022.
full_text:
Who is Mykhailo Drapatyi, Ukraine's new commander-in-chief?
- Published
Maj Gen Mykhailo Drapatyi, 43, has replaced Oleksandr Syrskyi as Ukraine's commander-in-chief - the third since the start of Russia's full-scale invasion in 2022.
His nomination has been welcomed by both civil society and the military. Drapatyi's name was chanted during protests that started off backing his friend, ex-defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov, but ended up demanding Syrskyi's dismissal.
"There's no better person for this position nowadays in Ukraine," one Ukrainian soldier told the BBC.
Drapatyi's support rests on years of military experience in post-Soviet Ukraine, his skills as field general and his reputation for being a humane and strong commander among the military.
He graduated from the Kharkiv Institute of Tank Troops in 2004 and began serving as a lieutenant.
Ten years later he gained prominence when footage went viral showing his infantry fighting vehicle smashing through a makeshift barricade.
It was May 2014 and pro-Russian separatists had taken over parts of eastern Ukraine, when Drapatiy's battalion entered the southern city of Mariupol to free hostages held in the city's police department.
He later recalled being told there were barricades more than a metre high ahead and being asked what to do. "I said, let's take it by storm. This video flew around the world," he said in an interview.
Later that year, he was commended for withdrawing encircled Ukrainian units from a border area of the Luhansk region.
Drapatiy returned to university in 2021 for further operational and strategic training and was presented with a sword of honour as top graduate in June 2021 by British ambassador Melinda Simmons.
When Russia's full-scale invasion began in February 2022, Drapatiy was deputy commander of joint forces.
He led operational groups - temporary task forces - in several areas of the front line, successfully pushing back the advance of Russian troops towards Kryvyi Rih and liberating a number of settlements in the Kherson and Dnipropretrovsk regions.
By 2024 he was heading the land troops of the Ukrainian army and leading task forces in some of the east's most intense combat areas.
Less than a year later, a training ground in the Dnipropetrovsk region was targeted by a Russian missile and 12 soldiers were killed and 60 others were wounded in the strike.
Drapatyi handed in his resignation the very same day, saying he took personal responsibility for the "conspiracy of silence and impunity" that had led to the deaths. "
"An army in which commanders bear personal responsibility for the lives of personnel keeps living. An army in which nobody is responsible for a loss dies," he wrote.
It was seen as a sign of personal accountability, and Zelensky's decision to instead appoint him commander of the Joint Forces of the Armed Forces of Ukraine was widely praised.
From then on, whispered rumours of tensions with Syrskyi grew louder.
"Drapatyi is a relatively young general. He is gifted. He was always sent to places where the situation was extremely difficult," one unnamed officer told Ukrainian media in June 2025. "I do not think he has political ambitions. Yet I am sure his ambitions are not confined to the position of commander of the ground forces or the Joint Forces."
Just over a year later, Syrskyi has gone, and hopes for Drapatyi are high.
"Drapatyi has a very good reputation among the rank and file - especially those who joined after 2022 as civilians," says Mykola Bielieskov, senior analyst at the Ukrainian NGO Come Back Alive. But he notes Drapatyi will have to operate under serious constraints.
"The Commander-in-Chief has a lot of leverage. But war is a combination of government, the president's office, military suppliers, dependence on [Western] partners... so he's got a tricky path before him."
Prospects of a ceasefire with Russia remain slim and Ukraine faces another harsh winter of war.
Mobilising manpower is a priority, and Drapatyi will also be expected to tackle the corruption that touches all levels of the army, from conscription officers to defence procurement.
Meanwhile, he will have to capitalise on Ukraine's remarkable technological advances and the burgeoning tech defence industry that has spearheaded Ukraine's recent battlefield successes.
In his first message after being appointed Commander-in-Chief, Drapatyi acknowledged the difficulty of his task and promised to work "without making loud promises, with responsibility for our decisions, and with respect" for those on the front line.
Many will be looking for a change from what was seen as Syrskyi's "outdated" way of fighting, which placed little value on human life in favour of brutal offensives.
"It's a major role and people will expect change quickly," analyst Bielieskov said, warning against "oversimplification" that can lead to demand for sweeping improvements in an unrealistic length of time.
This has been echoed by former interior ministry adviser Oleksiy Kopytko. As commander-in-chief, he noted, "you are worshipped and loved by all today, not loved by everyone tomorrow, and are guilty of everything the day after tomorrow, with none of your achievements mattering".
Valery Zaluzhnyi, who was removed as army chief in 2024, predicted that Drapatyi would "have a very difficult time. Much harder than he imagines".
But among many soldiers and ordinary Ukrainians there is a tangible sense of excitement for the new shift in outlook that Drapatyi represents. One said that if Mykhailo Fedorov were reinstated as defence minister, his and Drapatyi's leadership would be "Russia's worst nightmare".
When he resigned from his position in 2025, Drapatyi listed issues he had tackled in the Ground Forces - ranging from combat training reform to unfair mobilisation, corruption and flawed procurement systems.
"There is expected resistance, but efforts need to be stepped up," he said at the time.
He will face similar problems in his new role - albeit on a much larger scale and under the eyes of the whole country.

title: 'It makes me different': Meet the women breaking world records in lumberjack sports
summary: The BBC finds out what is driving the sports' increasing popularity with women and what it takes to be the best.
full_text:
'It makes me different': Meet the women breaking world records in lumberjack sports
- Published
Karolina Urbanova had never heard of lumberjack sports until a new neighbour moved into her small Czech village and enlisted her help for events when she was a teenager.
Now 24, she has just broken two world records at the annual Lumberjack World Championships, which were held over the weekend in Hayward, Wisconsin.
The competition, which Hayward has been hosting since 1960, brings people from across America and around the world together to showcase their skills in everything from logrolling, chopping and sawing to speed climbing.
Men and women mainly compete separately but some events are mixed.
This year, 40 women from across the US and abroad joined 66 male competitors – a far cry from the female representation Urbanova saw when she started out.
"There were maybe like three girls doing this sport in Europe," she tells the BBC, adding: "Telling people from the city that you are chopping wood usually every day, they looked weird at me."
"It makes me different … so it is what it is."
Urbanova was talent-spotted by a male competitor alongside her mother and sister and they began training weekly in a barn - trying out different axes and techniques and getting pointers from more experienced athletes as they entered competitions throughout Europe and further afield.
She discovered she was fast, and her new records prove it. In the Women's Standing Block category, where an axe is used to speed-chop through an upright, vertical block of wood, she cut through 9in (22.8cm) of white pine in 19.38 seconds. The previous record was 21.17 seconds.
In the Women's Underhand Chop, where competitors stand on a piece of wood and chop between their feet, she cut through 11in of white pine in 21.28 seconds. The fastest previous time was 24.26.
Urbanova is perhaps the quintessential example of lumberjack sports' expanding reach, particularly among women. She says that while they are niche in America, they're nearly unheard of in the Czech Republic.
That is not the case for Meredith Ingbretson, a Hayward native, who also broke a record at the world championships – winning the Women's Boom Run, where competitors race back and forth across eight linked cedar logs. Her time was 13.78 seconds – less than a second faster than the previous record of 13.98.
She said she'd buckled down in the past year - cutting out alcohol and anything else that "didn't align" with achieving her long-held goal.
Ingbretson was introduced to lumberjack sports at age three. They are a big part of life in Hayward, which was founded on the timber industry in 1880. It is a place where, as Ingbretson puts it, every resident "has probably been in logrolling lessons at least for one summer".
She has now been competing in logrolling for 28 years and began sawing and chopping more recently.
The number of female competitors in lumberjack sports has more than trebled in the past 30 years, according to Samantha LaSalle, event director of the Lumberjack World Championships. She's been involved with the sports since she was five, and her six-year-old daughter is already following in her footsteps.
While women have taken part in the world championships since the inaugural event in 1960, they were originally limited to logrolling. Getting them entry into chopping and sawing block events as well took time, LaSalle explains.
The Women's Standing Block [Chop], for instance, which Urbanova set the new record for, was only added in 2022.
"They [women] were saying: 'We can do more. We can do this event that the men have traditionally done'," said LaSalle.
"And as more of them practiced and got competitive in it, we said, you know what? There's enough gals that can do this, and do this at a high level, and we need to allow them to do that just like the men do.
"Now we're seeing those times drop each year - which just shows you how much better everyone is getting."
Both Urbanova and Ingbretson are fuelled by the love of competing and train all year - lifting weights, jogging, doing other cardio and refining their axe skills. They are also drawn by the familial and collegiate atmosphere, as well as the ability to travel and make friends around the world.
Prize money is rarely enough to cover all expenses when attending international competitions - the Wisconsin championships paid out $1,000 (£748) to the winners of each category, for example - so Urbanova stayed with a host family in Wisconsin.
Ingbretson and her husband, who also competes, were hosted in the Australian state of Tasmania last winter, while her mother put up Canadian and Australian competitors in Hayward for this year's world championships.
"I think that's something special … you can go somewhere and they'll let you stay and train you and work with you," Ingbretson said. "It's a very welcoming and open community. It's just so fun to be a part of."
She was also bolstered to see women continuing to compete even as their families grow.
"There were three or four mums [log]rolling this year, and so I think it's so cool to see that... they're still being competitive rollers or choppers."
Word of mouth and exposure - particularly through social media - have played integral roles in promoting the sport with women, organisers and competitors say.
"There are a lot of colleges across the US that have timber sports, and they're teaching and getting men and women into the sport of lumberjacking," said Ingbretson, who works as the community education director at Hayward's high school and manages a local fitness centre.
She says she's been treated like a celebrity at school and in town this week and finds it particularly gratifying when she's congratulated by young, up-and-coming competitors in the sport.
"It's just another reason to be active and engaged in the community that we are in, whether it's bringing in new kids or supporting the kids that just started [log] rolling."
Now, she's setting her sights on an all-round title.
"To be efficient in multiple disciplines…is very important, and it's very difficult ... it just takes a level of dedication and commitment to make it happen."
Urbanova, meanwhile, also hopes her success is inspiring and that she keeps up her record-setting streak.
"I'm still growing and still learning, but now the level of the girls is really high, so it's also hard to keep the same rhythm with them because they now want to be better than me," she said.
"I just feel pretty proud of myself."
