title: Trump Weighs ‘Massive Attack’ as Iran Rejects Cease-Fire Proposal
summary: President Donald Trump said Iran is “not ready” to make a deal and hasn’t “received enough pain yet.”
full_text:
It appears there will be no hasty retreat from weeks of escalating attacks between the U.S. and Iran, which have destabilized energy markets yet again.
On Thursday, President Donald Trump told Axios that he is weighing restarting major combat operations in Iran. Trump said he could carry out even larger strikes than the Operation Epic Fury strikes that killed dozens of Iranian leaders and started the war on Feb. 28.
“I am considering a massive attack. Bigger than ever before. I am close to making a decision. We are all set for it,” Trump said, adding that he knows there would be consequences to such an attack and that a final determination has not been made. The President said Israel “would join in two minutes” if asked but that “we don’t need anybody.”
Trump also said that Iran is “not ready” to make a deal and that its leaders “have some evil intentions.” Trump’s remarks came after Iran reportedly rejected a 15-point cease-fire proposal from the U.S. that was delivered by Iraq on Wednesday.
Trump appeared to suggest that the U.S. may escalate its attacks on Iran in order to force it to the negotiating table.
“They haven’t received enough pain yet,” Trump told Axios.
Tensions around the Strait of Hormuz
The sticking point appears to be the Strait of Hormuz, which Iran had militarized at the start of the war, halting commercial shipping and skyrocketing energy prices around the world. The June 17 U.S.-Iran memorandum of understanding did not definitively answer the question of the Strait; instead it said Oman and Iran would carry out discussions over management of the narrow waterway. Since the start of the war, Iran said it wants to manage passage through the Strait, including possibly charging fees. Trump has also at times suggested that the U.S. could take over control of the Strait and charge tolls.
Days after the MOU was signed, Iran resumed attacks on commercial ships in the Strait. The U.S. retaliated with strikes on Iran. The U.S. has escalated its attacks since, carrying out daily strikes on Iran for the past two weeks. Trump has also repeated his threats to attack Iran’s civil infrastructure, including power plants and bridges, and to “wipe out” Iran’s Revolutionary Guards, while Iran has vowed to avenge the death of its Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.
Iran has claimed responsibility for attacks on Gulf states since the MOU, citing retaliation for the U.S. strikes. The Associated Press reported a series of explosions near a military base in northern Iraq on Friday after the U.S. military had concluded its 13th consecutive night of strikes on Iran.
Tensions have escalated in recent days after Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen began attacking Saudi ships in the Red Sea, threatening to disrupt another maritime chokepoint. If shipping through the Bab-el-Mandeb Strait in the Red Sea halts, the world could face more economic pain. Already, Brent crude topped $100 a barrel on Thursday for the first time since May, and could climb further if the conflict continues to escalate. Trump warned on Thursday that “the U.S. will hold Iran responsible” for any further Houthi attacks, and that “major military punishment will be inflicted upon Iran and, of course, the Houthis, themselves.”
Iranian officials reportedly said they were not interested in any new deal that left the issue of the Strait unresolved.
Butting heads
Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi visited Tehran on Thursday and was expected to convey the U.S. position after he visited the White House last week. But U.S.-Iran negotiations seem off the table for now.
“The problem is not passing messages,” Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi told state television on Thursday. “The problem is America’s outlook, which is illogical, greedy and controlling.”
Israel has also continued attacks on Lebanon despite multiple U.S.-brokered cease-fire agreements. More than 4,000 people in Lebanon have been killed by Israel since March 2, according to the Lebanese Health Ministry. Analysts previously told TIME that Israel’s attacks could stand in the way of any longstanding peace with Iran, as Iran has repeatedly said any cease-fire deal must include Lebanon.
Trump and Iranian officials have butted heads on other issues. Trump threatened on Thursday to use frozen Iranian funds to pay for any damage to ships. The assets, that are under U.S. sanctions control, were meant to be released to Iran as part of the MOU.
Araghchi said on Friday that “seizing another nation’s assets to pay for unrelated future claims is an incendiary precedent.”
“Ensuing chaos will not be pretty or peaceful,” he added.

title: Meet Me in the Notes App
summary: Notes have staying power, writes Rainesford Stauffer, as vulnerable chaos, a counterpoint to hyper-curated feeds.
full_text:
“What’s the oldest note in your phone?” my younger sister asked, in the same tone one might use to share gossip. She was explaining what she called “notes app digest,” rereading notes like a kind of personal magazine of one’s own insight and nonsense.
I immediately scrolled. For better or worse, my notes app is the piece of technology closest to looking like the inside of my brain: a bit chaotic, annoyingly detail-oriented, and perhaps perpetually nostalgic. While handwritten to-do lists hold my life together, my notes app contains the catch-all, the weird (one that simply says “possum”), and the important (a list of people’s birthdays) coexisting.
Somehow, the mess of my notes resists all forms of optimization, or even coherence. Venturing back into our notes app isn’t just about fishing out that one password we swore we’d remember, or realizing we drafted a resignation letter in the same note as a reminder to get toilet paper. They are weirdly human markers of time, who and where we’ve been. Amid the endless push to optimize, streamline, and summarize our thoughts, notes have staying power.
For years, people have observed the delightful, vulnerable chaos of the notes app as a counterpoint to hyper-curated feeds. Charley Locke, writing for The Atlantic in 2024, noted that the app is “essentially built-in scratch paper on a phone, and it reveals a person’s digital subconscious.” A 2025 piece by Elahe Izadi for The Washington Post asked strangers to reveal the contents of their notes apps, an act somewhere between a confession and a grand reveal.
There are many reasons why people still default to writing notes, according to Dr. Bart Wojdynski, professor of journalism at the University of Georgia and director of the Digital Media Attention and Cognition Lab. It’s easy to use, and the icon connotes the idea of jotting on a post-it. “Maybe there’s an extent to which the basicness of the notes app also makes it feel less like it’s being read by our online overlords and used to market you ads,” Wojdynski says. (He noted he hadn’t read the user agreement in a bit, but it might feel “less likely that it’s being scraped to feed some LLM somewhere”). “I think this is related to people trying to have digital copies of their memory,” Wojdynski adds.
Recently, when looking back through notes, Andy Carr, 37, a PhD candidate and part-time adjunct instructor in New York, found something in addition to those for grocery shopping or lesson planning for college courses he teaches. In summer 2020, Carr, his brother, and his sister-in-law were navigating end-of-life care for his mother. There was a jumble of memories, from notes of contacts that hospice care nurses passed along to one reading “Skippy pb jingle—send writer to prison,” a vent about a peanut butter commercial that ran incessantly on the TV at home as the family worked to make his mom comfortable and provide as much physical help as they could.
Revisiting those notes, Carr found affirmation. For years after his mother’s passing, he struggled with feeling that he froze up at the time. The notes showed specific examples of all he had been present for and engaged with around his mother’s death, all of the things he’d taken down as important information to ensure nothing slipped through the cracks. He never deletes messages or notes, he said, and usually, rarely goes back to them: “But little things like this make me really grateful that I can.”
Nadia De Ala, 37, a leadership and negotiation coach who moved to Mexico from the Bay Area two years ago, still has the first note she ever put in the app in 2016: a poem she remembers writing while dreading her commute to a previous job. “I really feel like it’s a time capsule, because it keeps a lot of memories, the essence of who I’ve been at every iteration and season of my life,” she says, adding that it’s even interesting to look back on foods she liked to grocery shop for.
Our phones, in other words, can augment our memories. Julia Soares, assistant professor of psychology at New Mexico State University, says that devices can become “partners for helping us remember things.”
“You’ll find some very heartfelt things that are digital,” she explains, adding that sometimes people don’t think of these “digital scraps or mementos” as being particularly valuable, but many people hold onto voicemails or even emails.
Recently, over coffee, one of my dearest friends took me on a tour of her meticulously organized notes. If my notes app functions as the junk drawer of my mind, hers was like opening the door to different beautiful rooms: a list of good things that are happening, checklists for household maintenance, and a folder of notes her sister assembled of their mom’s recipes, complete with videos: a living cookbook. In our conversation, my sister talked about her own notes app discoveries: goals she’d written down only to be met with surprise at how much she’d grown since then, or the minutiae of everyday life she documented for no obvious reason. Other people shared their own earliest notes: addresses of apartments they were touring, passages of favorite books they kept for inspiration, a compliment they’d received, nonsensical thoughts that somehow got funnier the longer they kept them.
A slingshot backward through a scroll, and I meet: Myself from 2017 who saved a recording of her childhood cat purring; 2019 me, writing interview questions for my first book; my 2022 self nervously drafting multiple iterations of the same message asking for her stuff back at the end of a relationship; me in 2024, who apparently was fleetingly into logging everything she baked.
Look at this mess, I think, as I thumb through 1,781 half-baked thoughts, drafts, memories, and past selves. What chaos. I could never delete her.

title: How NATO Is Quietly Reinventing Itself for Trump
summary: NATO has been quietly reshaping itself toward America’s preferred vision of European security.
full_text:
The portents were not good. Before departing for the recent NATO summit in Ankara, President Donald Trump took to Truth Social to berate the alliance. He posted figures suggesting the alliance was a financial burden on the United States. He complained about allies neither contributing their fair shares nor standing with America. And he deemed it ridiculous for the U.S. to continue along this “one-sided” path.
Things didn’t improve when Trump touched down. During his first press conference at the summit, he singled out the big European allies—France, Germany, Italy, and the United Kingdom—for their lack of support over Iran. He reprised the demand that the Danish territory of Greenland be ceded to American control, and bashed the allies for insufficient defense spending. Trump suggested the allies were lucky to have him, claiming he only showed up as a favor to his “friend,” Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan.
Yet a day later, the mood had changed. Trump departed Ankara praising “the love” among the allies. He was seduced by a carefully orchestrated procession of prime ministers and presidents of member countries of the alliance, each in turn swallowing hard and praising his leadership. They were following a script already played to great effect by NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte, who has helped NATO survive Trump by perfecting the art of flattering the American president.
“Teflon Mark” and the art of the deal
When Rutte was appointed by the allies, he was not the obvious choice. As Dutch prime minister, he had led a country with a poor record of defense spending. There was also a strong argument at the time that NATO ought to select its first female Secretary General, or its first from an Eastern European ally.
But Rutte’s skill as a consensus-builder elevated his standing. Rutte had led Dutch coalition governments for nearly 14 years, and his reputation for deal-making and political survival had earned him the nickname, “Teflon Mark.” Crucially, for these reasons, Rutte also enjoyed the support of the Biden White House.
Rutte began work at NATO in Oct. 2024. Trump entered the White House for the second time three months later. Armed with an already well-honed gift for flattery, Rutte spared little time in cozying up to the incoming American president. At every opportunity since, he has praised Trump’s leadership. European and Canadian defense spending increases have, in Rutte’s telling, became the “Trump trillion.” He has an unerring ability to deflect difficult questions at press conferences—recently on Iran—so as to spare America any embarrassment.
When a Danish journalist accused him in Ankara of lacking self-respect for failing to counter Trump’s claims to Greenland, Rutte replied by comparing Trump’s impact on NATO to that of President Dwight D. Eisenhower, NATO’s first Supreme Allied Commander Europe and early advocate of fair transatlantic burden sharing. Trump rewarded Rutte by praising him as an “extraordinary person” and a “smart leader.”
Rutte’s unstinting support of Trump does carry a cost. Calling Trump “Daddy” at NATO’s 2025 Hague summit was cringeworthy for many diplomats. And sometimes Rutte’s spin on events rankles national sensitivities: his talking up of flights flown from bases in Italy to support Operation Epic Fury, the American war against Iran, recently drew a public rebuke from the Italian defense ministry. In January, Rutte intervened to set up a framework for discussing the Greenland question, prompting the Danish defense minister to point out that Rutte could not negotiate on Denmark’s behalf.
These reservations aside, Rutte remains, for now, an asset for the alliance: someone who can smooth over Trump’s impetuosity. NATO leaders understand his relationship with Trump is one of convenience, not political affinity. Rutte has worked tirelessly to support NATO’s broader agenda: standing up to Russia, supporting Ukraine, and, in his words, promoting “a stronger Europe in a stronger NATO.”
And Rutte is not averse to praising other NATO leaders. He commended German Chancellor Friedrich Merz for his “political courage” in ramping up German defense spending, and days before the NATO summit complemented then-British Prime Minister Keir Starmer for his “leadership” on Ukraine.
NATO’s savior?
Is it, then, too much to claim that without Rutte, NATO would be doomed? Similar questions were asked about Rutte’s predecessor, the Norwegian Jens Stoltenberg. As Secretary General during Trump’s first term, Stoltenberg too had an uncanny ability to read Trump’s mood and shield the allies from criticism.
Serious academic work has argued that Stoltenberg was, in part, responsible for NATO’s survival. Stoltenberg had to manage an American president who felt NATO was playing the U.S. as a sucker. In his memoirs, Stoltenberg recalls fearing, at the 2018 NATO summit, that the alliance “was about to stop functioning” if Trump made good on his threats to withdraw the U.S. security guarantee.
A deal brokered by Stoltenberg and Rutte—then at the summit as Dutch prime minister—kept Trump on board. Flattery, again, was the device. At the summit, Stoltenberg credited Trump’s strong leadership on defense spending for NATO’s revival.
What these examples suggest is that Secretary General of the NATO is no shrinking violet. Of the 14 office holders to date, five have been foreign ministers and two have served as defense ministers. The last three—Rutte, Stoltenberg, and his predecessor, the Dane Anders Fogh Rasmussen—came to the job as sitting prime ministers.
That standing allows the Secretary General to hold his own with NATO’s national leaders and with the alliance’s military commanders—the Supreme Allied Commander Europe and the Chair of the NATO Military Committee. The Secretary General can draw on considerable bureaucratic advantage: he heads up the International Staff at NATO headquarters, oversees the alliance’s polished public communications operation, and serves as the chief organizer of NATO summits.
But the Secretary General cannot countermand the nations. And here, ultimately, the U.S. carries the greatest influence. Despite his reservations, Stoltenberg could not prevent the U.S. from terminating NATO’s mission in Afghanistan in 2021. Today’s U.S. troop drawdowns in Europe, even if they directly affect NATO’s conventional defenses, are decided in the White House and the Pentagon. It is Rutte’s job to cast them in a positive light.
A shape shifting NATO
America has been critical of burden-shirking among the allies since NATO was formed. Trump has turned that sentiment into a weapon. Deference and sweet-talk have been Europe’s disarming response. It doesn’t always work: cozying up to the president—as Italian premier Giorgia Meloni recently found out—does not preclude a Trump tongue-lashing. Yet flattery did work in Ankara. Rutte deserves credit as the flatterer-in-chief.
Still, sycophancy only gets you so far. Practical measures aligned with American preferences are also needed. Away from the political theater, in recent months, the alliance has been quietly reshaping itself toward America’s preferred vision of European security: a “NATO 3.0.” Its chief architect, U.S. Under Secretary of War for Policy, Elbridge Colby, has spoken of the allies assuming “primary responsibility” for the conventional defense of Europe.
To that end, Europeans and Canadians are spending colossal sums on their militaries, and funneling more arms and aid to Ukraine, now that the U.S. is reluctant to do so. The transatlantic alliance may, as a result, be entering terra incognita.
The U.S. remains embedded in NATO’s command structure and is the ultimate guarantor of allied security through extended nuclear deterrence, but an unprecedented process of the Europeanization of NATO is under way. And it could fulfil America’s original vision for the alliance: that it serve as a framework within which Europe, as the historian Marc Trachtenberg has written, would be “able t

title: TikTok’s protection of minors should not be opt-in, warns EU
summary: TikTok has attracted the ire of the European Union over its protection of children who use the video sharing platform. The European Commission announced preliminary findings today under the Digital Services Act (DSA) that offer specific issues to address. The Commission suggests that TikTok should adjust the default settings of minors' "public" accounts so the […]
full_text:
TikTok has attracted the ire of the European Union over its protection of children who use the video sharing platform. The European Commission announced preliminary findings today under the Digital Services Act (DSA) that offer specific issues to address.
TikTok’s protection of minors should not be opt-in, warns EU
‘A high level of protection should not be an opt-in; it should be the default.’
‘A high level of protection should not be an opt-in; it should be the default.’
The Commission suggests that TikTok should adjust the default settings of minors’ “public” accounts so the content they post is only visible to TikTok users the teen has chosen to share it with, and that such content shouldn’t be recommended to other users in the For You feed. Even accounts set to private can be easily discovered through the ‘following’ lists of other users, and their profile photos can be seen by anyone. If TikTok fails to address the concerns, it could face a DSA non-compliance decision that imposes fines of up to six percent of the company’s global annual revenue.
“Minors deserve a safe experience from the moment they go online. The Digital Services Act requires platforms to build protections for minors into the design of their services, and holds them to account when they fail to do so,” EU tech chief Henna Virkkunen said in the announcement. “A high level of protection should not be an opt-in; it should be the default. This is our responsibility for current and future generations of European children.”
The preliminary findings follow UK communications regulator Ofcom launching a similar child safety investigation into TikTok last week, with updates expected in October. The EU says its separate probe to evaluate the addictive “rabbit hole effect” of TikTok’s recommender systems is still ongoing.

title: Facebook considers giving up and becoming TikTok
summary: Facebook is planning some big changes to try and keep its users from jumping to rival social platforms like TikTok - changes that sound dubiously similar to becoming a TikTok clone. Facebook head Tom Alison announced today that the platform will begin testing a "reimagined experience" later this year that will put a subset of […]
full_text:
Facebook is planning some big changes to try and keep its users from jumping to rival social platforms like TikTok — changes that sound dubiously similar to becoming a TikTok clone. Facebook head Tom Alison announced today that the platform will begin testing a “reimagined experience” later this year that will put a subset of users into a “full-screen video the moment they open the app.”
Facebook considers giving up and becoming TikTok
It’s also imitating Reddit. And Craigslist.
It’s also imitating Reddit. And Craigslist.
Meta didn’t share examples of what its experimental new interface will look like, only that it will initially roll out to countries with a noted preference for video content, with a potential expansion planned for the US next year. These tests are driven by Facebook observing that “video is where conversations are happening, communities are forming, and even commerce is starting to take place” — placing Meta’s original social media platform at risk of falling behind. While Meta doesn’t break out specific user figures for its individual platforms, it collectively lost 20 million users in the first quarter of 2026, according to the company’s own data.
Facebook is reportedly still the most popular social platform globally, but YouTube is a close second, and TikTok isn’t far behind — it passed the 1 billion monthly users milestone just three years after launch, significantly faster than Facebook. Meta launched Reels for Instagram in 2020 to better compete with TikTok, and now it’s trying to do something similar with Facebook. This is after Alison told The Verge in 2022 that he sees “TikTok chasing Facebook,” rather than the other way around.
Facebook has grown into a hodgepodge of social and commerce services over the years, and now it’s also emulating similar rival platforms to improve its own user experiences. Today it’s launching Seller, a dedicated Craigslist-like app for Marketplace sellers to track performance, manage listings, and message buyers. Facebook also launched its Forum app earlier this year that provides a dedicated space for people to interact with Facebook Groups — similar to subreddit communities on Reddit.
Changes are also being made to Facebook’s user verification badges, which require a paid subscription to Meta Verified that starts at $11.99 per month. Now, Facebook says it’s offering a free verified badge that can be obtained by completing a “simple selfie verification” process, with the aim of helping users know that a profile is linked to a real person.

title: Saylor and team overhaul Strategy's bitcoin metrics as bear market persists
full_text:
Saylor and team overhaul Strategy's bitcoin metrics as bear market persists
New framework gives common shareholders a clearer view of net bitcoin exposure after preferred stock and convertible debt obligations
- Strategy’s net reserve stands at $36.6 billion after subtracting $6.8 billion of out-of-the-money convertible debt and $15.5 billion of preferred stock from its bitcoin and cash reserves.
- The revised mNAV permanently sets the equity issuance threshold at 1.0x, while a 3.22% BTC breakeven ARR would allow bitcoin gains to cover interest and preferred dividend obligations indefinitely.
Strategy (MSTR), the biggest corporate holder of bitcoin, has created a new market metrics framework, replacing gross BTC-based figures with net equivalents that take out the company's growing preferred stock and convertible debt obligations. The purpose of the new framework is to give common equity holders a more transparent overview of the company’s position. 
The metric overhaul is part of a broader pattern, with Strategy repeatedly refining its guidance over the past year as it grapples with a bear market that began in October. The company’s flagship preferred stock, STRC, trades near $85 and has not returned to its intended $100 par value since mid-May.
Bitcoin is currently trading at roughly $65,000, 50% below its all-time high, while MSTR sits 84% below its November 2024 peak. 
The first metric is the new "Net Reserve", which currently sits at $36.6 billion. That figure takes Strategy's $55.6 billion BTC reserve (843,775 BTC), adds $3.2 billion in USD reserves, then subtracts $6.8 billion in out-of-the-money convertible debt and $15.5 billion in notional preferred, the $22.3 billion in senior claims that rank ahead of common shareholders in any liquidation scenario.
The company has also updated its multiple to net asset value (mNAV) formula. Under the old accounting method, the accretion threshold would usually keep the company’s mNAV above 1.0x, making it increasingly difficult to know whether new share issuance was actually beneficial for existing holders. The new formula anchors that threshold permanently at 1.0x — if MSTR trades above it, issuing new shares adds BTC per share for all investors. 
According to the company, the formula is: MSTR Price, divided by Net Bitcoin Per Share, representing whether MSTR trades above or below Net Bitcoin Per Share after debt and preferred claims.
The BTC Floor ARR is the minimum sustained BTC growth rate over the credit structure's duration before restructuring becomes a consideration for the company. Currently, the BTC Breakeven ARR sits at 3.22%, meaning bitcoin only needs to appreciate faster than that rate annually for Strategy to fund all interest and dividend obligations through BTC gains alone, in perpetuity.
Strategy has also introduced new bitcoin market metrics, such as the premium to the 200-week moving average and the Fear and Greed Index.

title: Brazilian farmers tokenized dairy cows to get loans, bypassing bank lending limits
full_text:
Brazilian farmers tokenized dairy cows to get loans, bypassing bank lending limits
Smart collars monitor herd health in real time to prevent fraud, allowing local agricultural businesses to secure thousands in funding backed by livestock.
- Farmers in Paraná, Brazil, have tokenized 10 dairy cows on the B3 stock exchange, raising nearly $20,000 in credit backed by their livestock amid tighter bank lending.
- The project, led by agtech firm Cowmed, uses AI-powered tracking collars to create encrypted digital identities for each cow, preventing double-pledging and enabling cows to serve as movable collateral.
- Cowmed, which already monitors about 100,000 cows worth more than $395 million, expects up to 20% of its network to adopt this tokenized financing model, potentially unlocking $77.6 million in new agricultural credit as part of a broader push into real-world asset tokenization.
Farmers in Parana, Brazil, struggling to get banks to loan them cash, became the first to tokenize livestock and place 10 dairy milk cows’ tokens for trade on the country’s B3 national stock exchange. They generated nearly $20,000 in credit backed by their cattle, signaling the potential of tokenizing RWAs as a financing tool.
The dairy cow tokenization in Brazil is a world first and serves as a test in a real-world scenario in which farmers are facing increasingly stringent lending limits imposed by local banks on small agricultural businesses.
"We take the cow, which is a real and tangible asset, and transform it into a digital asset backed by a unique code monitored in real time,” Thiago Martins of Cowmed, a Brazilian Agtec company, told CNNBrasil recently.
Martins and his company did not immediately respond to a CoinDesk request for comment.
“This digitization allows for formal registration with B3 as a movable asset,” Martins added. “The process is simple and gives the producer an advantageous opportunity to finance themselves, opening a new alternative for collateral at a time of strong credit restrictions in agribusiness."
To turn cattle into trusted financial guarantees or collateral without requiring inspectors to visit the property, Cowmed equips cows with an AI-powered Smarty Collar. These collars constantly monitor health, behavior, and location. The raw data is then converted into an encrypted digital identity tied directly to the B3 credit agreement.
Continuous tracking of cattle prevents farmers from double-pledging the same cattle across multiple loans. It also includes built-in safeguards that allow the farmer to swap one dead cow for a live one.
Cowmed already tracks about 100,000 dairy cows across more than 1,000 farms. The herd is worth over $395 million. The company expects up to 20% of its network to adopt this tokenized financing model, unlocking $77.6 million in fresh credit for the agricultural sector.
McKinsey & Company forecasts market of tokenized assets to grow to about $4 trillion by 2030, and Standard Chartered projected $30 trillion by 2034. As of March 2026, however, the total value of tokenized assets stood at $25 billion.

title: EU hits Russia with massive 21st sanctions package targeting $120B crypto network
full_text:
EU hits Russia with massive 21st sanctions package targeting $120B crypto network
The EU is considering a ban on third-country crypto services providers for the first time and is targeting 14 crypto companies, which it has not named yet.
- The European Union has expanded its Russia sanctions to target the A7 cross-border payments network, including its new links to Africa, and the A7A5 stablecoin used for sanctions evasion.
- The latest package widens a transaction ban to 14 crypto-related platforms in countries including Georgia, the UAE and Panama, and introduces a tool that could allow a full ban on crypto-asset services used by Russia.
- Alongside the digital asset measures, the EU is freezing assets and banning transactions for 94 banks and major financial institutions, and extending its transaction ban to 33 additional Russian credit and financial institutions.
The European Union (EU) extended sanctions against Russia to include four designations related to the cross-border A7 network, including its new links to Africa.
The EU is also extending its transaction ban to 14 unnamed crypto-related service platforms based in Georgia, Panama, the United Arab Emirates (UAE), the Marshall Islands, Kyrgyzstan and Belarus.
Chainalysis recently noted that on the A7 network, where the A7A5 stablecoin operates, has processed nearly $120 billion to date and that it is purposely built for Russia’s sanctions evasion.
"We’re hitting over a hundred banks and crypto operators, 40+ vessels in Russia’s shadow fleet, and several oil refineries in Russia and Belarus," Kaja Kallas, High Representative for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy and chair of the Foreign Affairs Council, said in a statement.
The EU announced its previous package of sanctions against Russia in April, saying it was the “biggest package” of sanctions against the country in two years. In that statement, the EU said “Russia is becoming increasingly reliant on cryptocurrencies for international transactions.”
The new sanctions come just three days after Russia’s State Duma passed legislation establishing the country’s first comprehensive framework for regulating crypto with most of the rules slated to come into effect on Sept. 1. The law creates a legal framework for crypto exchanges, depositories, other digital asset providers as well as traders and investors.
The 21st sanctions package also sees the first introduction of a possible full third-country ban for crypto-asset services. This new instrument will enable the EU to ban any transaction between an EU operator and any crypto provider used by Russia.
Alongside the digital asset crackdown, the EU is imposing asset freezes and a prohibition to make funds available to 94 banks and major financial institutions. It is extending its transaction ban to 33 additional Russian credit and financial institutions.

title: Crypto market maker B2C2 held sale talks with multiple potential buyers
full_text:
Crypto market maker B2C2 held sale talks with multiple potential buyers
The SBI-owned crypto trading firm is said to have attracted takeover interest from a number of suitors over the past 18 months, but valuation has been a sticking point.
- B2C2, the crypto market maker 90% owned by SBI Holdings, has held takeover talks with several potential acquirers over the past 18 months, according to sources
- The discussions have been hindered by valuation. B2C2 is said to be seeking a price of more than $1 billion, which one source said would be difficult to achieve in the current crypto market.
- The reported talks come amid a wave of consolidation across the digital asset industry, as firms pursue acquisitions to expand institutional offerings and scale in a maturing market.
B2C2, the crypto market maker 90% owned by Japan's SBI Holdings, has held takeover talks with several potential acquirers over the past 18 months, according to five people with knowledge of the matter.
Valuation has been a sticking point in the discussions, said two of the people, who spoke on condition of anonymity because the matter is private.
The London-based firm is said to be looking for a valuation in excess of $1 billion one person said, adding that such a deal would be difficult to pull off given the current crypto-market environment.
Discussions have centered on the sale of part or all of the company, though it is unclear whether any talks remain active.
A B2C2 spokesperson declined to comment. SBI did not respond to a request for comment by publication time.
Founded in 2015, B2C2 is an institutional cryptocurrency market maker and liquidity provider that enables banks, exchanges, brokers, hedge funds and asset managers to trade digital assets efficiently. The firm uses proprietary trading technology to provide deep liquidity and 24/7 execution across spot, derivatives, structured products and over-the-counter (OTC) markets.
Crypto markets have struggled for much of the year as weaker trading volumes, concerns over the economy and fading risk appetite weighed on digital assets. The tougher backdrop has hurt market makers, whose revenues depend largely on trading flows and providing liquidity. With spot trading volumes subdued, firms across the sector have faced pressure on profitability.
Mergers and acquisitions are expected to remain a defining theme in 2026 as digital asset firms consolidate to achieve scale, expand product offerings and meet growing institutional demand, according to industry analysts.
Exchanges, market makers, custodians and financial technology providers are looking to acquire complementary businesses to build integrated digital asset platforms, reflecting the maturation of the crypto ecosystem into a more institutional and regulated market.
SBI Financial Services, a subsidiary of SBI Holdings, acquired a 90% stake in B2C2 in December 2020, months after investing $30 million in the firm.
B2C2's financial results are not disclosed separately. They are reported as part of SBI's broader crypto-asset business segment. For the fiscal year ended March 31, that segment generated 89.6 billion yen ($550 million) in revenue, up 10.9% from a year earlier, while profit before tax was unchanged at 21.2 billion yen.
SBI Holdings said last month it had agreed to buy cryptocurrency exchange Bitbank for around $289 million.

title: A quantum roadmap would push Bitcoin much higher: Charles Edwards
summary: A Bitcoin development roadmap that addresses quantum computing risks could see the price surge by “double digits” very quickly, according to Charles Edwards.
full_text:
A quantum roadmap would push Bitcoin much higher: Charles Edwards
A Bitcoin development roadmap that addresses quantum computing risks could see the price surge by “double digits” very quickly, according to Charles Edwards.
Bitcoin developers need to swallow their pride and outline a clear plan to harden the blockchain against quantum computing attacks, according to Capriole Investments founder Charles Edwards. He says the day they finally bite the bullet, the price will respond very quickly.
“If the Bitcoin core team says in two or three months: ‘this is our roadmap, we’re gonna solve it in the next two years, these are the rough steps we’ll take,’ that would be amazing news,” Edwards tells Cointelegraph on Trade Secrets.
“I think that would discount a lot of the risk pretty much overnight,” Edwards says.
The question of whether Bitcoin developers should modify the network to make its cryptography quantum-resistant has sparked heated debate within the Bitcoin community, with some arguing that major changes could conflict with Bitcoin’s core ethos. Others claim quantum computers are many years away, and a rushed cure could be worse than the disease.
Charles Edwards says a clear roadmap could push price up “very quickly”
Edwards often highlights the risk of quantum computing to Bitcoin to his 132,800 X followers. The fear is that, one day, powerful enough quantum computers could break the cryptography that protects the Bitcoin network and potentially compromise Bitcoin wallets.
The uncertainty has impacted investor sentiment, and some analysts say it has contributed to the downfall in Bitcoin’s price. The world’s largest asset manager, BlackRock recently pointed to quantum computing as a potential long-term risk in materials for spot Bitcoin ETF investors.
However, Edwards says if Bitcoin developers outline a clear roadmap to address the quantum threat, as some other chains have already done, it could send Bitcoin’s price higher “very quickly.”
Source: Charles Edwards
“Double digits probably,” Edwards predicts. He adds the quantum issue is “somewhat counterintuitively an upside catalyst potential,” because it is currently on the back burner and the Bitcoin Improvement Proposals (BIPs) to date are “not really” a genuine solution.
Edwards is no stranger to making high-conviction calls on Bitcoin. Based in Melbourne, Australia, he founded Capriole Investments in 2019, a hedge fund focused on Bitcoin and digital assets. The firm uses a combination of quantitative models, AI, and macroeconomic analysis to guide its investment strategy across crypto markets.
Related: StarkWare CEO suggests 4% annual Bitcoin inflation to replace 21M cap
Charles Edwards says Bitcoin is 40% below its fair value
A growing number of observers worry the risk could become more serious if Bitcoin developers fail to make the necessary changes to the network before 2030. Ethereum is due to complete it’s post quantum overhaul by 2029, which will shine a spotlight on Bitcoin’s own preparations.
Bitcoin is trading at $65,270 at the time of publication. Source: CoinMarketCap
Edwards estimates that Bitcoin is currently around 40% below what he considers its fair value based on energy value, while arguing that quantum risk accounts for roughly a 30% discount. “That means it’s more than priced in,” Edwards said. Bitcoin is trading at $65,270 at the time of publication, roughly 49% below its October all-time highs of $126,100.
Edwards clarifies that Bitcoin’s current price reflects the quantum risk based on the information available today, rather than any unknown future developments that could accelerate the threat and tank the price further.
His estimate is based on the timelines outlined by leading quantum computing companies and researchers for when “Q Day” could arrive, the point at which quantum computers become powerful enough to reverse engineer private keys from public keys.
“That sits in that four to five year range, give or take, a few years,” Edwards says.
Edwards says he also factors in the time Bitcoin would need to develop and implement a solution, which BIP-360 author Ethan Heilman estimates could take years.
“If we’re gonna get into maths, it’s pretty simple; it is just an aggregation of those expert opinions. So it’s based on that, and based on the fact that there’s currently no solution for Bitcoin.”
“That risk again falls significantly if there’s a solution or if there’s a roadmap to a solution. But it also could grow if tomorrow we find out that Google is, you know, twice as far ahead on their roadmap to Q Day or some other major company,” he said.
“It’s priced in today, but it’s not to say that it can’t get worse or better. It’s just I think it’s skewed more probabilistically to the upside from here,” Edwards says.

title: Thailand SEC files complaint against Bitkub over alleged false disclosures
summary: Thailand’s SEC filed a criminal complaint against Bitkub and two former directors over alleged false disclosures linked to a 2021 cyberattack involving $50 million in assets.
full_text:
Thailand SEC files complaint against Bitkub over alleged false disclosures
Thailand’s SEC filed a criminal complaint against Bitkub and two former directors over alleged false disclosures linked to a 2021 cyberattack involving $50 million in assets.
Thailand’s crypto industry is facing fresh regulatory scrutiny after authorities accused Bitkub, one of the country’s largest digital asset exchanges, of providing false information to regulators.
Thailand’s Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) filed a criminal complaint against Bitkub Online and two former directors over alleged false reporting connected to a 2021 cyberattack, the regulator announced on Thursday.
The complaint names former Bitkub directors Sakolkorn Sakavee and Thaweesap Rawan, who the SEC said were responsible for submitting company reports during the period under investigation.
The case comes as Bitkub’s parent company considers a potential public listing, putting renewed attention on transparency and governance at one of Thailand’s most prominent crypto businesses.
SEC alleges Bitkub failed to disclose impact of hack
The SEC said a cyberattack in May 2021 resulted in the theft of 16 types of digital assets from Bitkub, worth about 1.7 billion baht ($50 million).
The regulator alleged that Bitkub later replaced the stolen assets by Oct. 31, 2021, but failed to accurately reflect the impact of the incident in its daily net liquid capital reports.
According to the SEC, reports submitted between May 10 and Oct. 30, 2021, did not show a significant reduction in the exchange’s assets following the theft.
Former Bitkub directors Sakolkorn Sakavee (left) and Thaweesap Rawan. Source: Bangkok Post
The regulator alleged that the omission gave the impression that customer assets remained unchanged and that the exchange had not suffered losses from the attack.
The SEC accused Bitkub and the former directors of violating multiple provisions of Thailand’s digital asset regulations over the alleged false disclosures. The case will now proceed through investigation, possible prosecution and court proceedings.
Bitkub says disclosure delayed to prevent bank run
Bitkub disputed the SEC’s allegations in a post on X, saying the case stems from disclosure decisions made after the May 2021 cyberattack rather than fraudulent conduct. The exchange said it delayed disclosing the wallet compromise to prevent a bank run while it addressed the loss of the stolen assets.
The company said its co-founders later purchased equivalent digital assets to cover the stolen funds, leaving neither the company nor its customers with financial losses. The company added that it has since strengthened its governance, compliance and security systems.
Related: Bank of Thailand targets USDT and cash flows in gray money crackdown
Founded in 2018, Bitkub has emerged as one of the largest crypto exchanges in Thailand. According to CoinGecko, the platform ranks first among Thai crypto exchanges by trust score and had about $712 million in daily trading volume at publishing time.
Source: CoinGecko
In December 2025, Bitkub confirmed to Cointelegraph it was considering an initial public offering (IPO), including a potential listing in Hong Kong.
Cointelegraph reached out to Bitkub for additional comment on the SEC’s complaint and its IPO plans but had not received a response by publication.

title: RWAs become Hyperliquid’s largest trading category
summary: Tokenized RWA trading became Hyperliquid’s largest trading category for the first time, accounting for more than half of the decentralized exchange’s weekly trading volume.
full_text:
RWAs become Hyperliquid’s largest trading category
Tokenized RWA trading became Hyperliquid’s largest trading category for the first time, accounting for more than half of the decentralized exchange’s weekly trading volume.
Perpetual decentralized exchange (DEX) Hyperliquid’s weekly trading volume in tokenized real-world assets (RWAs) exceeded that of all other asset categories combined for the first time.
RWAs generated $25.1 billion in trading volume from July 13 to July 19, accounting for 52% of Hyperliquid’s total weekly volume of $48.2 billion, according to Blockworks data.
“Hyperliquid’s RWA market alone was larger than the combined crypto perpetual volume of every other DEX,” wrote ARK Invest’s research director for digital assets, Lorenzo Valente, in a Thursday X post.
The milestone reflects growing demand for tokenized assets on Hyperliquid. Over the past month, RWA holders grew by 32% to 1.25 million users, while the total value of tokenized RWAs rose by 3.5% to $36.7 billion, according to data aggregator RWA.xyz.
Hyperliquid generated $7.6 million in revenue over the past week, according to DefiLlama. The perp DEX ranked third among crypto applications by weekly revenue, behind stablecoin issuers Tether and Circle, which generated $112 million and $45 million, respectively.
Hyperliquid: Perpetual Futures Volume, 2-year chart. Source: Blockworks
Related: Hyperliquid launches prediction markets for real-world events
Major “structural shift” for crypto markets: Circle co-founder
Crypto-native firms and traditional financial institutions have expanded tokenized asset offerings as they bring more financial assets onto blockchain networks. In March, the NYSE partnered with tokenization platform Securitize to develop blockchain-based stock trading infrastructure with 24/7 trading and settlement.
Circle co-founder and CEO Jeremy Allaire said growing RWA trading on Hyperliquid marks a “major structural shift” in crypto markets, moving “away from speculating on endogenous digital commodities,” in a Friday X post.
Earlier in July, Pantera Capital said perpetual futures could become a dominant trading instrument beyond crypto, as perps offer structural advantages over traditional derivatives, including 24/7 trading, no contract expiries, simpler position management and continuous price discovery.
Hyperliquid’s growth has drawn attention from Wall Street institutions, including NYSE parent Intercontinental Exchange (ICE), whose CEO, Jeffrey Sprecher, urged regulators to create a “level playing field” for launching 24/7 onchain perpetual futures contracts.

title: Arthur Hayes, BitMEX co-founders face fraud claims over alleged ‘Insider Trading Desk’ as exchange winds down
summary: BitMEX, Arthur Hayes, Samuel Reed and Benjamin Delo face a proposed class action alleging insider trading and deliberate server freezes.
full_text:
Arthur Hayes, BitMEX co-founders face fraud claims over alleged 'Insider Trading Desk' as exchange winds down
Quick Take
- Two former BitMEX customers sued the exchange and its founders on Thursday, alleging BitMEX operated what they described as a hidden “Insider Trading Desk” that traded against its own users and froze servers during volatile stretches to trigger liquidations.
- The plaintiffs claim losses of roughly 623 bitcoin between them and are seeking return of the coins in kind rather than cash damages.
We'd love your feedback.
Two former BitMEX customers filed a proposed class action against the crypto exchange and its three co-founders on the same day the platform announced it would shut down permanently in September 2026.
BKX Services Inc. and David Namdar allege that BitMEX operated an undisclosed "Insider Trading Desk" that traded against its own customers using private account data.
The pair also claim that the exchange deliberately froze its servers during periods of high volatility to lock users out while forcing liquidations, according to the complaint filed in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York.
Thursday’s suit names Arthur Hayes, Samuel Reed, Benjamin Delo and former head of business development Gregory Dwyer as defendants, alongside HDR Global Trading Limited and four affiliated entities.
What the plaintiffs say happened
The complaint alleges BitMEX liquidated positions when unrealized losses reached roughly half of posted collateral, despite remaining collateral still exceeding the losses.
Plaintiffs claimed the exchange set that trigger higher than needed to protect itself, seizing remaining collateral and routing it into the platform's Insurance Fund.
Dwyer ran the Insider Trading Desk from BitMEX's Manhattan office throughout 2018, the plaintiffs claim. They allege the desk used software to identify which price movements would liquidate the most customers, then placed trades to induce those moves.
BitMEX told users that hidden orders were concealed from other traders and that liquidation points stayed private, according to the filing. The complaint alleges the Insider Trading Desk saw all of it, and that BitMEX created burner accounts paired with generic email addresses to disguise its own trading.
The plaintiffs also allege the exchange manipulated prices on third-party reference exchanges to force liquidations on its own platform.
The March 2020 lockout
The complaint points to March 13, 2020, when customers were locked out of the platform for roughly 25 minutes and about $800 million in leveraged positions were liquidated.
BitMEX attributed the outage to a hardware issue with its cloud provider that day, then said four days later that two distributed denial-of-service attacks were the root cause, according to the filing. The plaintiffs allege the freezes were deliberate and that customers were never compensated.
The claimed losses
BKX Services says it lost at least roughly 305.8 BTC across 13 liquidations between July and August 2018. Namdar, who traded under an alias, claims about 316.9 BTC in losses across 14 named liquidations plus at least 69 smaller ones, spanning August 2019 to May 2020.
The two counts are replevin and fraud. Replevin seeks return of specific property rather than its cash value, meaning the plaintiffs want the bitcoin itself back. The proposed class covers anyone who bought bitcoin swap products on BitMEX in domestic U.S. transactions from July 23, 2018 onward. Plaintiffs estimate tens of thousands of members and put aggregate claims above $5 million.
An earlier case ended in dismissal
A substantially similar suit — Messieh v. HDR Global Trading — was filed in the same court in April 2020 under the Commodity Exchange Act. The parties stipulated to voluntary dismissal, and the court entered that order on June 30, 2025, without prejudice.
The plaintiffs argue the statute of limitations was tolled for the full stretch of that case, from April 2020 through June 2025.
BitMEX pleaded guilty in 2024 to violating the Bank Secrecy Act and was hit with an additional $100 million fine in January 2025, reportedly. President Donald Trump pardoned the co-founders in March 2025.
BitMEX said Wednesday it would cease operations on Sept. 23 at after 11 years, citing a strategic review by HDR's board without giving further explanation.
The complaint, filed before BitMEX publicly announced its planned shutdown, alleges that the exchange "continues to operate the platform without any repercussions."

🔐 BlackRock, Coinbase, and Strategy Back a $15 Million Bitcoin Quantum Defense Fund
Nine of the biggest names in finance and crypto formed the Bitcoin Security Consortium, pledging a combined $15 million over three years to fund Bitcoin security research and open-source development focused on quantum computing defense.
The members are BlackRock, Coinbase, Strategy, Anchorage Digital, ARK Invest, Block, Blockstream, Fidelity Digital Assets, and Galaxy. The consortium won’t hold or allocate the money, each member picks which developers and researchers to fund directly, and the group says it will not direct Bitcoin development or take positions on protocol changes. Mike Schmidt of the developer-funding nonprofit Brink will coordinate on a volunteer basis. BlackRock’s head of digital assets, Robert Mitchnick, said Core developers “do incredibly important work” and that the group would make more funding available for Bitcoin’s long-term security.
Quantum computers capable of breaking Bitcoin’s cryptography don’t exist today. But roughly 6.9M BTC ($450B) sit in addresses that would be vulnerable if one arrives, and any fix requires coordinating changes across wallets, exchanges, miners, and users, which takes years. That’s why work is starting now on proposals like BIP 360, a new output type designed to limit public key exposure, alongside post-quantum signature schemes.
It makes sense for this particular group to back quantum defense research. BlackRock runs the largest spot Bitcoin ETF, alongside Fidelity and ARK. Strategy is the biggest DAT and holds 843,775 coins. Coinbase custodies much of the institutional supply and most of their products revolve around crypto trading. These firms have billions in client and shareholder exposure to an asset whose long-term security is now something they have to answer for—which makes funding Core developers cheap insurance.
It’s been widely known that the quantum risk to Bitcoin is a massive overhang for the foreseeable future, and many investors have come out and flatly said Bitcoin is not investable until quantum is solved. Many don’t believe the core BTC devs can move fast enough (and reach agreement) to make the type of changes needed to solve quantum in time. Enter those with the most skin in the game. title: India Orders GitHub to Take Down Jack Dorsey's Bitchat Amid Protests
summary: The order gave GitHub three hours to pull three code repositories, citing the messaging app's use during protest internet shutdowns.
full_text:
In brief
- India's Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) ordered GitHub to remove and disable three Bitchat code repositories within three hours, invoking the IT Act and the 2021 IT Rules.
- The agency said the Bluetooth-based, serverless app impedes lawful surveillance and could be misused during "public disorder, riots, terrorism," or internet shutdowns.
- Jack Dorsey published the notice, and digital-rights group the Internet Freedom Foundation called the takedown "unconstitutional and authoritarian."
India's cybercrime agency has ordered GitHub to take down the code for Bitchat, the decentralized messaging app built by Jack Dorsey, giving the Microsoft-owned platform three hours to comply.
The notice, issued Thursday by the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) under the Ministry of Home Affairs, named three repositories under the "permissionlesstech" account—the main Bitchat project, its Android build, and the Android releases page—and invoked Section 79(3)(b) of the IT Act, 2000 and Rule 3(1)(d) of the 2021 IT Rules. It told GitHub to "remove and disable access" to the code without vitiating any evidence.
the government of india does not like technologies like bitchat and wants it taken down pic.twitter.com/gjzMg1NGCi
— jack (@jack) July 24, 2026
Bitchat routes messages directly between nearby phones over Bluetooth mesh networks, with no internet, servers, phone numbers, or accounts—a design I4C said "significantly impedes lawful interception, attribution, and investigation." The agency warned the app could be exploited during "public disorder, riots, terrorism, organized crime, or internet shutdowns," and cited provisions of the IT Act and the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, India's criminal code.
'Cockroach' protests
The order lands as India wrestles with a youth-led movement over exam-paper leaks. Tens of thousands have rallied in Delhi behind the satirically named Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), and Prime Minister Narendra Modi has vowed fast-track courts for officials accused of rigging exams. With mobile internet cut around Parliament and the Jantar Mantar protest site, demonstrators turned to offline tools such as Bitchat.
Dorsey, the former Twitter chief and Block CEO, posted the notice with a terse line that the "government of india does not like technologies like bitchat," while the Bitchat Community account said that “Governments that fear people talking without permission will always go after the tools that make it possible.” The Internet Freedom Foundation condemned the order as "unconstitutional and authoritarian," arguing it named no unlawful content and bypassed India's blocking procedures.
India is not the first state to move against the app. China ordered it pulled from Apple's App Store in April, echoing Beijing's 2023 ban on Dorsey's Nostr-based Damus. Removing an app from a store limits distribution, while removing the source code tries to kill a project outright—though open-source code can be freely copied and mirrored.
Indeed, just hours after India’s crackdown, Bitchat repos were mirrored to decentralized code collaboration platform GitLawb. Days earlier, Dorsey's Block launched Buzz, a decentralized platform pitched as a way to cut its own reliance on GitHub. Microsoft has not said whether it met the three-hour deadline.

title: OpenAI’s new voice mode makes it to the ChatGPT desktop app
summary: ChatGPT Voice on desktop can work with both ChatGPT Work and Codex to complete tasks and control agents.
full_text:
OpenAI on Thursday said it has updated its ChatGPT desktop app to add support for ChatGPT Voice, allowing users to talk to the app to control AI agents and perform tasks on their computer.
The new feature taps OpenAI’s new family of voice models called ChatGPT-Live, which it launched earlier this month.
OpenAI said ChatGPT Voice works with both ChatGPT Work and Codex, and can also tap computer use skills to look up websites and apps. Plus, on macOS, with Appshots, users can let the app access what’s on their screen, including alt-text.
At launch, ChatGPT Voice’s smartphone version featured smoother conversations, with better interruption handling, but it was not built to take action on smartphones.
Thursday’s desktop update is more capable, allowing users to dictate complex commands involving many steps, and respond when ChatGPT needs their input.
In a demo video, OpenAI showed a developer asking ChatGPT to create a new thread, make a pull request, and find the root cause for a bug, with one command.
The company said that users can utilize ChatGPT Voice in Codex from the iOS app through remote access.
Anthropic has also updated its voice mode for Claude, which can tap the company’s Opus, Sonnet, and Haiku models to complete tasks in apps like Gmail, Calendar, Slack, Notion, and Canva.

title: Facebook launches a dedicated Marketplace app for sellers, adds a free verification system
summary: Seller is a dedicated Marketplace app for people who list and sell items frequently.
full_text:
Facebook is rolling out updates today in a bid to increase engagement and make the platform more organized for its users. In the offing are new apps for sellers on Marketplace; a verification system to prove you are human on services like Dating, Marketplace, and Groups; and a new immersive design for video.
Facebook Marketplace sees more than 430 million monthly listings, and with more than 1.1 billion active users, it is a big reason younger folks still use the platform.
To keep this momentum going, Facebook is launching a separate app for people who list and sell items on the platform frequently. Dubbed “Seller,” the app lets sellers manage their listings, message buyers, and track the performance of items.
Facebook is also rolling out a free verification system called Facebook Verified — not to be confused with Meta Verified, which lets you subscribe for a verification mark and other features.
The new system lets people take a selfie to verify their authenticity as a real user, and then the verification mark will show up on their profile across Facebook Dating, Marketplace, and Groups. The verified mark looks like a check mark within a white circle, unlike the blue badge you can get by paying for Meta Verified.
The company said it is also testing an optional, immersive, full-screen video view for the Facebook app that pops up as soon as you open it. This update will initially be rolled out to “video-heavy” international markets, and make its way to the U.S. next year.
Facebook said users can turn off this UI to go back to the feed-based interface. The company has tested a similar update with Instagram in several markets.
New app releases are turning into a routine course of action for Meta, which has ramped up its app development to engage different sets of users. In May, it debuted a Reddit-like app for Facebook Groups called Forum, and this month it released a vibe-coding app called Pocket.
The company said it plans to add AI to the app to help users automate tasks such as writing descriptions of items they want to put up for sale, or search through groups to answer questions.

title: Robot snakes searched for Venezuela earthquake survivors in collapsed buildings
summary: US robotics researchers flew to Venezuela with snakebots after getting a call.
full_text:
Robots slithered like snakes into the rubble of collapsed buildings to search for trapped survivors in the aftermath of Venezuela’s double earthquake disaster.
The so-called snake robots represented a unique technological aid for international search and rescue efforts following two earthquakes that struck Venezuela on June 24, killing more than 5,000 people and leaving behind 16,740 injured. Rescuers from around the world used trained dogs, seismic and acoustic listening devices, video cameras on sticks, or thermal imaging cameras to search for signs of survivors—but the snakebots equipped with a video camera could squeeze through tight spaces to search deep within fallen building debris.
“The reason why snake robots are useful is they can get into tightly packed volumes that machinery and people otherwise cannot, and that’s important in search and rescue because we were able to extend the visual reach of the rescue workers in a safe way,” Howie Choset, head of the Biorobotics Lab at Carnegie Mellon University in Pittsburgh, told Ars. “In a sense, you’re doing minimally invasive surgery on a structure with a snake robot.”
Each 4-foot-long snakebot is modular in design with individual body segments that can be swapped out and easily replaced or upgraded. A human operator directs the robot using a video game controller and a control case laptop tethered to the robot, but software algorithms allow the robot to autonomously coordinate the body segments for the appropriate body movements when being directed to travel from point A to B.
Choset and his colleagues have spent nearly two decades developing different versions of the snake robots that can explore archaeological sites, swim underwater and even assist with minimally invasive surgery. But they first put the snake robot to the test in search and rescue scenarios following an earthquake that struck Mexico City on September 19, 2017, when they helped search a collapsed apartment building.

title: DEX Aggregator Odos Winds Down, Urges Users to Move Assets Before Month End
summary:
The company behind the swap aggregator says the app goes read-only on July 27 and shuts down for good on July 30, leaving users a narrow window to secure their funds.

The post DEX Aggregator Odos Winds Down, Urges Users to Move Assets Before Month End appeared first on Unchained.
full_text:
The company that operates Odos, a decentralized exchange aggregator that has routed more than $100 billion in cumulative volume, is shutting down.
“After much consideration, the operating company behind Odos is winding down its operations,” the team said in a statement posted Thursday. “The app moves to read-only on July 27, and all Odos services shut down permanently on July 30, 2026.”
New account signups, wallet creation, and limit orders were switched off as of the announcement, though existing users can still swap and close out positions, according to the statement.
“There will be no further development, support, or maintenance from the team,” Odos said.
Move Your Assets First
Odos user funds stay on-chain and under their owners’ control, the team said. However, users who created a wallet through Odos using a social or email login need to transfer their assets to another wallet or export their private key before July 30. The team said wallet access and step-by-step instructions will remain available at its official page after the shutdown.
The ODOS token is a separate matter. The team said it exists on-chain independently of the operating company, adding that it does not custody or market-make it and the closure does not change the token’s mechanics. The Odos DAO, also separate from the company, is also expected to communicate its own plans in due course.
A Warning About Scams
The team, warning against scams, stressed that there will be no new products, token migrations, claims, or airdrops. “Anyone promoting these via DM, ‘support’ accounts, or ‘migration’ websites is a scammer,” it wrote in the thread, adding, “Never share your seed phrase or sign transactions from links claiming to be Odos.”
Odos launched in 2022 as a spin-out of venture incubator Semiotic Labs.

〈比特幣教科書級買單現身！量化交易員：幣安護盤團隊回歸，造市商正「搶跑」進場〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
比特幣（BTC）市場底部訊號浮現？據具備 7 年經驗的知名量化交易員 Killa 於 X 平台發文指出，比特幣訂單簿目前出現了教科書級別的設置。他觀察到「幣安防止暴跌團隊」疑似回歸，大量巨額買單緊跟在當前價格下方，這通常會促使造市商與演算法暫時搶先進場。
（前情提要：砸盤預警？貝萊德 IBIT 轉出 3,126 枚比特幣至 Coinbase，價值逾 2 億美元）
（背景補充：比特幣選擇權「看跌情緒消散」！Glassnode：Put/Call 比率急降，防禦部位大解除）
隨著比特幣（BTC）近期走勢震盪，市場資金的細微變化正成為投資人判斷後市的關鍵指標。台北時間 7 月 24 日稍早，擁有 7 年經驗的知名量化交易員 Killa（@KillaXBT）在社群平台 X（前 Twitter）上分享了一張比特幣訂單簿圖表，直指當前市場出現了他過去屢次見證的「教科書級設置（Textbook setup）」。
Textbook setup on $BTC.
Seen this occur numerous times.
"Binance plunge protection team is back. Usually, when large bids start trailing just below price, MMs and algos tend to front run them temporarily." https://t.co/pn57qaBChQ pic.twitter.com/tbE6Q8sBzx
— Killa (@KillaXBT) July 24, 2026
「幣安護盤團隊」再現？巨額買單緊跟幣價
Killa 在貼文中指出，他觀察到訂單簿中出現了極具特徵的流動性佈局，並形容這代表著「幣安的防止暴跌團隊（Binance plunge protection team）又回來了」。他特別引用了自己今年 6 月 5 日的舊文來強調，這並非單一的偶發事件，而是市場上反覆出現的一種特定模式。
所謂的「防止暴跌團隊」通常被社群用來戲稱那些在價格下跌時，於關鍵價位佈置龐大防守買盤的巨鯨或主力機構。當這類強大的買盤力量介入時，往往會對短期的價格行為產生顯著的托底作用。
演算法與造市商的「搶跑」效應
深入解析這種模式的運作機制，Killa 解釋道：「通常情況下，當大量比特幣買單開始緊跟在價格下方時，造市商（MMs）和演算法往往會傾向於暫時搶先交易（Front run）。」
這意味著，巨額的底部掛單為市場提供了強大的支撐預期，導致高頻交易機器人與造市商為了避免錯失低價籌碼，或是防範潛在的急遽反彈，會選擇在這些巨型買單真正成交前，就主動進場掃貨。這種搶跑行為能在短期內迅速推升或穩住幣價，形成技術面上的反彈訊號。
社群多空分歧：下探 5 萬還是上看 8 萬？
儘管訂單簿上出現了強烈的支撐訊號，但該貼文下方的社群留言卻顯示出多空雙方的嚴重分歧。有看空交易員悲觀預估比特幣將下探至 50,000 美元水平；另一名用戶 @nafis_sheikhh 也認為，即使有巨大買單護航，幣價跌至 54,000 至 55,000 美元的機率依然很高。
相反地，看多者如 @LokiLouke 則認為，只需給多頭一點時間醞釀，比特幣有望反彈至 76,000 至 80,000 美元區間。他甚至預測，在傳統金融市場經歷修正後，比特幣將以更快的速度恢復，並上看 85,000 美元大關。

title: 美英官方報告：中國 Kimi K3 安全攻防能力「明顯落後」美國頂尖 AI 模型
summary:
美國國家標準與技術研究院（NIST）與英國 AI 安全研究所（UK AISI）今日聯合發布了一份備受矚目的初步 […]

〈美英官方報告：中國 Kimi K3 安全攻防能力「明顯落後」美國頂尖 AI 模型〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
美國國家標準與技術研究院（NIST）與英國 AI 安全研究所（UK AISI）今日聯合發布了一份備受矚目的初步評估報告。針對中國新創 Moonshot AI 最新推出的 Kimi K3 模型，測試結果顯示其在漏洞利用與網路攻擊能力上，雖然擊敗了先前的開源王者 GLM-5.2，但整體表現依然「明顯落後」於美國最頂尖的閉源前沿模型。
（前情提要：自託管 AI 模型更省錢？Cline 實測 Kimi K3 成本優勢，網反駁：按任務算比 Fable 5 貴）
（背景補充：擠爆！Kimi K3 上線 48 小時用量達上限，月之暗面暫停新訂閱）
隨著人工智慧模型的能力不斷突破，其在網路安全攻防上的潛力與威脅已成為各國政府的高度國安焦點。台北時間 7 月 23 日，隸屬於美國 NIST 的 AI 標準與創新中心（CAISI）與英國 UK AISI 發布了一項針對中國 Moonshot AI 旗下最新模型 Kimi K3（預計於 7 月 27 日開放權重）的聯合網路安全能力評估報告。這份官方報告的發布，不僅是一次技術實力的檢驗，更是美中兩強在 AI 領域角力的具體展現。
CAISI’s latest blog post evaluates Kimi K3 and its cyber capabilities.
Based on a preliminary cyber-focused evaluation, Kimi K3 performed significantly below the leading U.S. frontier AI models.https://t.co/r9K3Pp0IiH
— U.S. Department of Commerce (@CommerceGov) July 23, 2026
高難度漏洞利用，Kimi K3 掛零
這份初步評估報告首先聚焦於模型的「漏洞利用開發能力」。在名為 ExploitBench 的公開基準測試中，測試人員要求模型針對 41 個 2023 年後的 V8 引擎（Chrome 瀏覽器核心）漏洞進行攻擊演練。結果顯示，Kimi K3 的整體成功率約為 32%，雖然勝過此前最具網路能力的開源模型 GLM-5.2（約 24%），但面臨最高難度挑戰時卻暴露了實力差距。
報告指出，Kimi K3 在這 41 個測試樣本中，完全無法達成最具破壞性的「任意程式碼執行（ACE，Arbitrary Code Execution）」。相較之下，參與測試的頂尖美國模型平均能在約 20 個樣本中成功達成 ACE，展現了輾壓級的漏洞利用能力。
企業網路攻擊模擬：僅走到一半進度
除了單一漏洞利用，評估團隊還透過「The Last Ones（TLO）」基準測試，模擬了一場包含 4 個子網路、約 20 台主機的 32 步企業網路攻擊場景（人類專家約需耗時 20 小時）。
測試數據顯示，Kimi K3 平均只能推進到第 17 步的攻擊進度，而美國最先進的閉源模型平均能完成到第 28.5 步。更殘酷的是，過去只有少數閉源模型能徹底解決 TLO 測試（成功率約 6 至 7 成），而 Kimi K3 在 10 次嘗試中，僅有 1 次能在 1 億個 token 限制內成功走完這 32 步的完整攻擊鏈。
安全防護形同虛設，美商務部發文宣傳
這份報告的另一個重大發現，在於 Kimi K3 內建的系統級安全防護機制（safeguards）顯然不夠嚴謹。測試人員發現，這些防護措施並未能有效阻止該模型協助開發代理式的網路漏洞利用工具，甚至無法擋下其嘗試執行進攻性的網路操作。
報告發布後，美國商務部官方帳號 @CommerceGov 隨即在 X 平台發文，強調「Kimi K3 的表現明顯低於領先的美國前沿 AI 模型」。儘管 Kimi K3 在開源/開放權重模型中已展現出超越 GLM-5.2 的進步，具備一定攻擊弱防護企業系統的能力，但這份由美英官方背書的成績單，無疑是向世界宣告：在最核心、最具破壞力的 AI 網路安全技術上，美國仍穩坐霸主地位。

title: 砸盤預警？貝萊德 IBIT 轉出 3,126 枚比特幣至 Coinbase，價值逾 2 億美元
summary:
據鏈上數據分析帳號 Onchain Lens 於今（24）日發布的最新監測指出，資管巨頭貝萊德（BlackRo […]

〈砸盤預警？貝萊德 IBIT 轉出 3,126 枚比特幣至 Coinbase，價值逾 2 億美元〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
據鏈上數據分析帳號 Onchain Lens 於今（24）日發布的最新監測指出，資管巨頭貝萊德（BlackRock）旗下的比特幣現貨 ETF（IBIT）錢包，已將高達 3,126 枚 BTC（價值約 2.03 億美元）轉移至 Coinbase Prime。這筆鉅額資金的挪動隨即引發社群熱議，擔憂是否為機構拋售或應對客戶贖回的潛在賣壓訊號。
（前情提要：比特幣選擇權「看跌情緒消散」！Glassnode：Put/Call 比率急降，防禦部位大解除）
（背景補充：機構砸盤訊號？Abraxas Capital 7 小時內向交易所轉入 1.97 億美元比特幣和以太坊）
隨著比特幣現貨 ETF 的資金流向持續牽動市場敏感神經，華爾街資管巨頭的一舉一動都備受矚目。台北時間 7 月 24 日，據知名鏈上數據分析帳號 Onchain Lens 監測指出，貝萊德（BlackRock）旗下的比特幣現貨 ETF（IBIT）錢包出現大額資金異動，將價值超過 2 億美元的比特幣轉移至加密貨幣交易所 Coinbase 的機構平台 Coinbase Prime。
BlackRock moved 3.126K $BTC (~$203M) from its IBIT Bitcoin ETF wallet to Coinbase Prime.
The movement was executed across multiple transactions, including several 300 $BTC batches and one 126.168 $BTC transfer.@blackrock @coinbase pic.twitter.com/hD4ty5YARy
— Onchain Lens (@OnchainLens) July 24, 2026
分批轉出 3,126 枚 BTC，轉移細節曝光
根據 Onchain Lens 披露的鏈上數據，貝萊德本次總計轉出了 3,126 枚比特幣（BTC），若以當前市場價格估算，總價值約高達 2.03 億美元。這筆龐大的資產並非一次性轉出，而是透過多筆交易分批執行。
鏈上紀錄顯示，這些交易包含了數筆 300 枚 BTC 的批次轉帳，以及一筆精確至 126.168 枚 BTC 的單筆轉移。作為 IBIT 的官方加密資產託管方，Coinbase Prime 頻繁接收此類資金調度，但在市場情緒敏感的當下，鉅額轉帳依然挑動了投資人的神經。
轉入交易所引發社群「拋售」擔憂
由於資金是直接流向 Coinbase Prime，這項大額轉帳立刻在加密社群中引發熱烈討論。有社群用戶 @errmb786 便在貼文下方留言詢問：「這是否意味著準備拋售（does this indicate selling）？」
通常而言，巨鯨或機構將大量加密資產從冷錢包轉入中心化交易所，往往被市場視為潛在的賣出準備，或是為了滿足場外交易（OTC）的需求。不過，考量到 IBIT 作為合規的比特幣現貨 ETF，其資產調度通常與客戶的申購與贖回（Creation and Redemption）機制密切相關，或者僅是常規的資產託管重組與結算。
儘管如此，在市場行情波動之際，超過 2 億美元的流動性轉移仍值得投資人保持警戒。後續 IBIT 是迎來大規模淨流出，抑或只是單純的內部錢包整理，仍需密切觀察後續的 ETF 資金數據與比特幣價格走勢。

title: 歐盟第 21 輪制裁封殺俄羅斯加密後門！鎖定 1,200 億美元加密支付網路與 14 家平台
summary:
歐盟正式發布針對俄羅斯的第 21 輪大規模制裁方案，全面加強對加密貨幣規避制裁的打擊力度。據《CoinDesk […]

〈歐盟第 21 輪制裁封殺俄羅斯加密後門！鎖定 1,200 億美元加密支付網路與 14 家平台〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
歐盟正式發布針對俄羅斯的第 21 輪大規模制裁方案，全面加強對加密貨幣規避制裁的打擊力度。據《CoinDesk》報導，本次制裁鎖定處理高達 1,200 億美元交易的「A7 跨境支付網路」與其穩定幣，並將 14 家海外加密服務平台列入交易禁令名單。此外，歐盟更首度引入新機制，未來恐將全面封殺協助俄羅斯的非歐盟第三方加密業者，顯示打擊俄國金融命脈的決心。
（前情提要：俄羅斯國家杜馬今日決議加密貨幣法案！散戶年限買 30 萬盧布，最快 9/1 生效）
（背景補充：美國警告：俄羅斯計劃對波蘭發動武裝行動，以測試北約集體防衛決心）
在俄烏戰爭持續膠著之際，俄羅斯利用加密貨幣規避國際制裁的「金融後門」正成為西方國家的頭號打擊目標。據《CoinDesk》報導，歐盟（EU）已正式發布針對俄羅斯的第 21 輪大規模制裁方案，此次行動將重點聚焦於加密貨幣網路與數位資產服務提供商，意圖全面切斷俄羅斯的替代性資金管道。
瞄準 1,200 億美元支付網路與穩定幣
本次制裁的重中之重，是鎖定被指控專門協助俄羅斯規避制裁的「A7 跨境支付網路（A7 cross-border payment network）」及其發行的 A7A5 穩定幣。根據區塊鏈數據分析公司 Chainalysis 的資料顯示，該網路迄今已處理近 1,200 億美元的驚人交易量。
歐盟不僅對 A7 網路相關的四項指定目標實施制裁，更特別關注其近期積極拓展的「非洲連結」。與此同時，交易禁令也被擴大至 14 家未具名的加密相關平台，這些平台分散在喬治亞、阿拉伯聯合大公國（UAE）、巴拿馬、馬紹爾群島、吉爾吉斯及白俄羅斯等地。
首創「第三方封殺」機制，逾百家金融機構遭殃
為了徹底防堵漏洞，歐盟在第 21 輪制裁中首次引入了一項極具威脅性的新工具。這項新機制賦予歐盟權力，未來可能全面禁止任何歐盟實體，與協助俄羅斯的「非歐盟（第三方國家）加密資產服務提供商」進行交易。
歐盟外交與安全政策高級代表 Kaja Kallas 在聲明中強調：「我們打擊了超過一百家銀行和加密業者、40 多艘俄羅斯影子船隊的船隻，以及俄白兩國的幾家煉油廠。」在數位資產打擊之外，歐盟也同步凍結了 94 家銀行及主要金融機構的資產，並將交易禁令擴展至另外 33 家俄羅斯信貸與金融機構。
反制俄羅斯加密貨幣合法化
外界觀察指出，歐盟此次出手時機極具針對性。就在制裁發布的三天前，俄羅斯國家杜馬才剛通過該國首部全面的加密貨幣監管立法，旨在為加密貨幣交易所、託管機構及數位資產提供者建立法律框架，大部分規則預計將於 2026 年 9 月 1 日正式生效。
早於 2026 年 4 月，歐盟就曾發布過被稱為「兩年來最大規模」的制裁方案，並警告俄羅斯正日益依賴加密貨幣進行國際結算。隨著俄羅斯試圖將加密貨幣交易合法化並常態化以繞過國際金融系統，歐盟與俄羅斯在數位金融戰場的攻防，勢必將在未來幾個月內變得更加激烈。

〈比特幣選擇權「看跌情緒消散」！Glassnode：Put/Call 比率急降，防禦部位大解除〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
據知名鏈上數據平台 Glassnode 於官方 X 平台發布的最新貼文指出，比特幣（BTC）選擇權市場正逐漸褪去「防禦性」色彩。隨著比特幣價格在 67,000 美元附近企穩，選擇權的 Put/Call（賣權/買權）比率與短期偏度（Skew）皆出現顯著下滑，同時隱含波動率保持壓縮狀態。這暗示市場對於短期的下行風險擔憂正在消退，看漲情緒逐漸回溫。
（前情提要：比特幣失守 6.5 萬、ETH 回測 1870！爆倉 2.5 億鎂、恐慌指數續走低）
（背景補充：機構砸盤訊號？Abraxas Capital 7 小時內向交易所轉入 1.97 億美元比特幣和以太坊）
隨著比特幣（BTC）近期價格走勢逐漸回穩，衍生品市場的資金佈局也正悄悄發生轉變。台北時間 7 月 24 日，知名鏈上數據分析機構 Glassnode 於社群平台 X（前 Twitter）發布了最新的比特幣選擇權（Options）市場數據分析，深入剖析了隱藏在價格表象下的部位分布、波動率狀態以及市場情緒變化。
$BTC options are turning less defensive as put/call ratios and short-dated skew fall, while volatility stays compressed.
Here's what BTC options data reveals about positioning, volatility, and sentiment beneath the surface.👇 pic.twitter.com/tb458FNSwA
— glassnode (@glassnode) July 24, 2026
Put/Call 比率急降，看漲部位奪回主導權
根據 Glassnode 分享的圖表與數據顯示，比特幣選擇權未平倉量（Open Interest）的 Put/Call 比率出現了急劇的下滑，從 6 月底的約 0.76，大幅降至目前的約 0.52。這意味著，買權（Call）的未平倉量在整體市場中的佔比正在不斷擴大。
分析指出，這項數據變化的背後，傳遞出明確的市場訊號：隨著比特幣價格在 67,000 美元附近逐漸企穩，投資人過去一段時間所建立的「防禦性部位（Defensive positioning）」正在快速解除，市場正重新擁抱上漲的預期。
波動率維持壓縮，期限結構向上傾斜
在隱含波動率（Implied Volatility, IV）方面，比特幣的平值（ATM）隱含波動率在整個曲線上依然保持在相對壓縮的狀態。具體而言，1 週期的短期波動率約為 34.3%，而 6 個月期的長期波動率則落在 40.8%。
Glassnode 觀察到，這種「向上傾斜的期限結構（Term Structure）」顯示出，市場已經將近期的事件風險進行了折現（Discounted），投資人並不認為短期內會有引發市場劇烈波動的黑天鵝；不過，較長期的不確定性仍讓長天期選擇權保留了適度的防禦性溢價。
短期避險需求降溫，社群：給我綠蠟燭！
此外，用來衡量極端行情的「25-delta 偏度（Skew）」在前端也出現了急劇下跌。1 週期的短期偏度降至接近 4%，而 3 個月至 6 個月的中長期偏度則維持在 11% 到 12% 左右。這進一步證實了短期的下行避險需求正在大幅降溫，儘管長期選擇權仍未完全卸下防備。
有趣的是，儘管鏈上數據與選擇權指標透露出市場結構正在轉向樂觀，但並非所有投資人都買單這類深度的技術分析。知名社群用戶 @Devin_NFTHunter 就在該篇貼文下方直言：「選擇權數據很酷，但價格走勢才是王道。給我看綠蠟燭，不是比率。」道出了許多散戶渴望看到實質性價格突破的真實心聲。

title: AI 巨頭私下最怕什麼？Axios：擔憂遭惡意利用製造「致命病原體」，引發生化災難
summary:
據《Axios》知名專欄報導，當私下詢問 AI 架構師與科技領袖最擔心的風險時，多數人直指 AI 可能遭惡意利 […]

〈AI 巨頭私下最怕什麼？Axios：擔憂遭惡意利用製造「致命病原體」，引發生化災難〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
據《Axios》知名專欄報導，當私下詢問 AI 架構師與科技領袖最擔心的風險時，多數人直指 AI 可能遭惡意利用，製造出能無聲且快速傳播的致命病原體。一項最新調查更警告，若缺乏完善的防護措施，到 2030 年由 AI 導致逾百萬人死亡的災難性事件機率將超過 20%。
（前情提要：輝達vs AMD 正夯、CPU架構大對決，誰能定義AI智慧體新標準？）
（背景補充：Googel Q2 雲端收入飆漲82%！摩根大通：AI進入回報期，可逢低買進）
隨著人工智慧技術的高速發展，推動前沿模型進步的科技巨頭們，心中卻隱藏著對未來的深層恐懼。據《Axios》專欄「Behind the Curtain」最新報導指出，當私下詢問幾乎每一位 AI 架構師與領導者最擔憂的風險時，他們的答案出奇地一致：一種能悄無聲息、廣泛且快速傳播，讓人來不及阻止的致命病原體。
專家共識：AI 恐加速生化武器開發
專家們罕見地達成共識，認為先進的 AI 模型極有可能幫助惡意行為者，在各國政府與產業建立完善的防範系統之前，就輕易製造出致命病原體。隨著 AI 逐漸深入理解人類的生物脆弱性，這已被業界視為「合理可能」的重大風險。
麻省理工學院（MIT）FutureTech 與昆士蘭大學（University of Queensland）針對 272 位研究人員進行的一項最新調查，對 24 項主要 AI 風險進行了排名。結果顯示，若無任何緩解防護措施，到 2030 年 AI 危險能力導致災難性後果（定義為超過 100 萬人死亡或造成 1,000 億美元損害）的機率超過 20%；即使在有緩解措施的情況下，發生災難與 AI 啟用大規模傷害武器的機率也仍各有約 12%。
AI 巨頭連署警告，防護網成監管焦點
這項潛在的末日威脅並非空穴來風。上個月，包含 OpenAI 的 Sam Altman、Anthropic 的 Dario Amodei、Google DeepMind 的 Demis Hassabis、微軟的 Mustafa Suleyman 以及 Meta 的 Alexandr Wang 等科技領袖，才剛共同簽署了一封公開信，嚴正警告 AI 衍生的生物武器風險，並強烈呼籲加強保障措施。
專家擔憂，資源充足的惡意行為者可利用強大模型繪製人類生物脆弱性，找出能讓已知病原體更易傳播或對現有治療免疫的基因調整方案。在大量生物與基因組數據訓練下，AI 產生可行候選方案的速度，宛如數百位最聰明的科學家以超高速、不眠不休地工作。
隨後，這些方案便可利用越來越便宜的基因編輯工具進行合成。最終，這些新穎的病原體將在公共衛生系統察覺前就開始散播，其遏制難度將遠超過 COVID-19 時期。這也讓關於「開源模型」是否容易遭監管外濫用的辯論成為焦點，如何在推動技術進步與防範邪惡意圖之間取得平衡，將是全人類必須共同面對的嚴肅課題。
